["Enhancing forage production through Growth Booster: Natural growth regulators Auxin and Plant-Growth Promoting Rizobacteria to support forage availability for Ruminat. (National research and innovation agency, BRIN)", "2025", "The area of grassland is not increasing in size but is narrowing due to competition with food-based land, conversion of productive land functions, global warming, and forage land has not become the main focus in livestock activities. This causes the availability of forage to be difficult to fulfill. Feed management as one of the pillars of feed security, is urgent and absolute to be implemented so that the need for fresh forage for cattle which is the main source of energy and crude fiber can be met. Mini elephant grass, Gama Umami elephant grass, and Pakchong elephant grass have good biomass and forage quality. However, the pasture capacity for these grasses is still not optimal. To increase pasture capacity, growth booster technology needs to be implemented. Growth booster is a natural growth agent that can increase grass productivity up to two times. At the nursery production stage, natural growth regulators (ZPT) such as auxins play an important rolein the root growth process. This ZPT can stimulate root growth so that the rooting time of plants is faster. In addition, proper pasture management can affect forage production, quality and productivity. Utilization of Rhizobacteria through Plant-Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) can stimulate plant growth, can improve defoliation quality and yield. However, this technology is only adopted in agriculture and plantations, while in forage feed its use has not been implemented, so this becomes interesting and is an opportunity for the Research Team to conduct this research. This research will be carried out for 3 years. The first year consists of two stages, namely the first stage is to produce a nursery of 3 types of grass, namely mini elephant grass, Pakchong grass, and Umami elephant grass by giving natural auxin ZPT treatment. The nursery with the best production on each HPT in the first stage will then be continued to the second stage, namely planting (demonstration plot test) by applying PGPR at different levels. Year Two: the best results in Year One research will then be tested for multi-location adaptation in 2 districts, namely Barru and Enrekang districts. Year Three: in-vivo testing of cattle by giving Super HPT from the second year of research in two districts, namely Barru and Enrekang Regencies. The outputs that will be produced in this research are IPR in the form of Patents, and Reputable International Journals."]

["Eco-Friendly Eggshell Meal on Milk Yield and Quality of Holstein Friesian Cows", "2024", "Mineral deficiencies, particularly a lack of Calcium (Ca), can have a detrimental effect on the performance of livestock, including dairy cows. While commercial sources of Ca are commonly used in dairy cow feed, they may not always be available or affordable. In this regard, introducing a new approach that utilizes eggshell meal as a natural source of Ca can not only improve milk yield and quality but also reduce waste. Therefore, we experimented to evaluate whether an eco-friendly eggshell meal could be a viable alternative source of Ca for Holstein Friesian dairy cows and improve milk yield and quality. We used 20 cows (ethical consideration No. 470/UN4.6.4.5.31/PP36/2023) that were experimented with different levels of eggshell meal in a completely randomized design with five treatments and four replications. The experimental diets were as follows; eggshell meal 0%+ commercial mineral 100% (EM0+ CM100); EM 25%+ CM 75%; EM 50%+ CM 50%; EM 75%+ CM 25%; and EM 100%+ CM 0%. The results showed that the eco-friendly eggshell meal as a source of Ca increased the milk yield by up to 100%. The intake of dry matter and milk quality, such as pH, density, CP, and P, had a similar effect on commercial minerals. Therefore, eggshell meal could effectively replace commercial mineral supplements in the diets of Holstein Friesian dairy cows. Not only does this approach lead to increased milk yield and Ca content in the milk, but it also has the potential to reduce waste in eggshell production. By utilizing eggshell meal as a raw material for mineral source feed, dairy farmers can promote environmental sustainability and improve the efficiency of the dairy sector."]

["Enhancing Milk Yield and Quality of Holstein Friesian through Special Formulation Urea Molasses Multinutrient Block (Fundamental Research Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)", "2024", "The production of urea molasses multinutrient block (UMMB) typically involves cement and molasses. However, prolonged use of cement can lead to health issues in livestock, while molasses is often in short supply due to its extensive use as a raw material in various industries. Thus, alternative materials are highly needed as substitutes for both cement and molasses. This study assesses the effects of using cocoa pulp as filler and tapioca meal as an adhesive in UMMB production on Holstein Friesian dairy cows’ performance, milk yield, and milk quality. The experiment applied a complete randomized design (CRD) with three treatments, namely without UMMB supplementation (T0 as control), supplementation with 500g of regular UMMB (T1), and supplementation with 500g of UMMB made with cocoa pulp and tapioca meal (T2). Each treatment had five replications. The results indicated that UMMB supplementation significantly affected (p < 0.05) forage dry matter intake (DMI), total DMI, milk fat, and milk viscosity. Up to 50% of the molasses and cement used in UMMB production can be replaced with cocoa pulp and tapioca meal without reducing the final product’s physical quality. Substitution of molasses filler and cement adhesive with cocoa pulp and tapioca meal enhances forage DMI and total DMI while maintaining the yield and physical quality of milk in Holstein Friesian cows."]

["Production Performance and Milk Quality of Holstein Friesian Dairy Cow with the Utilization of Eggshell Meal Extract as a Source of Minerals (Unhas Internal Grant)", "2024", "Milk production hinges on high-quality feed; minerals are indispensable in concentrate feed. Eggshells, a readily available by-product, contain essential minerals like calcium (Ca), phosphorous (P), and magnesium (Mg). Our study investigated eggshell meal as a mineral source for dairy cows. We assessed different mineral sources\\' impact on Holstein Friesian dairy cows\\' performance, blood Ca levels, and milk\\'s macro mineral quality. The study employed a completely randomized design (CRD) with 3 treatments and 5 replicates, involving 15 Holstein Friesian dairy cows aged 4–5 years with an average weight of ±500kg. Treatments included commercial mineral source concentrate feed (T1), eggshell meal mineral source concentrate feed (T2), and eggshell meal extract mineral source concentrate feed (T3). Parameters included milk yield, dry matter intake (DMI), feed conversion efficiency (FCE), blood Ca levels, and milk quality. The study revealed that using eggshell meal significantly increased milk yield and FCE compared to commercial minerals. However, there were no significant differences in blood Ca levels, physical milk qualities (pH, specific gravity, and viscosity), chemical qualities (protein and fat), and Mg content. The eggshell meal extract treatment showed milk\\'s highest Ca, P, and K content. In conclusion, our findings support using eggshell meal and extracts as a valuable source of Ca minerals in dairy cow diets, providing a sustainable alternative to traditional mineral supplements."]

["Reproductive Physiology of Friesian Holstein Dairy Cows Supplemented with Mung Bean Sprouts at Different Levels (Fundamental Research Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)", "2024", "The productivity of Friesian Holstein (FH) cows in Indonesia is still low, this is influenced by the prolonged calving interval in post partum dairy cows resulting in low pregnancy success rates. One of the causes of low pregnancy success in dairy cows is reproductive tract disorders. Low pregnancy success rates can be overcome through improved feed and reproductive management to support increased population and productivity of dairy cows. Feed management that can be done is by providing additional feed of mung bean sprouts which have a high protein content. Mung bean sprouts have the potential to improve nutritional adequacy in livestock because they are rich in protein sources, vitamins, and minerals. The purpose of this study was to improve the reproductive physiology of FH dairy cows supplemented with mung bean sprouts at different levels. A total of 16 lactating dairy cows aged 4-5 years with a lactation period of 1-4 months. This study used a completely randomised design (CRD) with 4 treatments for each of the 4 replicates: Supplementation of mung bean sprouts 0% of concentrate (P0); Supplementation of mung bean sprouts 5% of concentrate (P1); Supplementation of mung bean sprouts 10% of concentrate (P2); Supplementation of mung bean sprouts 15% of concentrate (P3). Parameters observed were physiological responses (heart rate, respiration frequency, rectal temperature, and skin surface temperature), haematological values (HR, SDP, Hb, Ht, and platelets), and reproductive physiology (behaviour, vulva condition, speed of lambing, duration of lambing, and estrogen concentration). The results of this study showed that physiological responses had a significant effect (P<0.05) on rectal temperature but no effect (P>0.05) on heart rate, respiration frequency, and skin surface temperature. Haematological values had a significant effect (P<0.05) on platelets but no effect (P>0.05) on red blood cells (HR), white blood cells (SDP), haemoglobin (Hb), and haematocrit (Ht). In reproductive physiology, there was a significant effect (P<0.05) on oestrogen concentration but no effect (P>0.05) on behaviour, vulval condition, estrus speed, and estrus duration. The conclusion of this study is that supplementation of mung bean sprouts at different levels on physiological responses (heart rate, respiration frequency, and skin surface temperature) has no effect but can increase rectal temperature, haematological values (HR, SDP, Hb, and Ht) has no effect but decreases platelets, and reproductive physiology (estrus behaviour, vulva condition, estrus speed, and estrus duration) has no effect but can increase estrogen hormone concentration."]

["Economic Feasibility and Health Parameter of Holstein Friesian Calves Fed Whey-Dangke Fortified Green Calf Starter (Fundamental Research Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)", "2024", "This research evaluated the impact of feeding green calf starter fortified with whey-dangke on Holstein Friesian dairy calves\\' Health parameters and Economic Feasibility. Experimental diets were applied to 18 Holstein Friesian dairy calves using a randomized complete factorial design with two factors: type of calf starter and level fortification of whey-dangke. The results showed that calves fed different types of calf starter, the level of whey-dangke fortification, and the interaction between the two factors had no significant effect (P>0.05) on physiological, hematological, and blood biochemical. However, the alanine aminotransferase (ALT) parameter had an interaction; the ALT values in the green calf starter treatment fortified with 5% whey-dangke exhibited a highly significant difference (P<0.01) compared to the green calf starter treatment fortified with 2.5% whey-dangke, as well as the conventional green calf starter fortified with both 2.5% and 5% whey-dangke. The level of whey-dangke fortified significantly affected ADG, FCR, and feed cost per unit of gain (p<0.05). The use of whey-dangke was able to increase ADG and decrease FCR and feed cost per unit of gain. In addition, physiological, hematological, and blood biochemical profile values of Holstein Friesian Friesian dairy calves remained within the normal range when fed whey-dangke-fortified green calf starter."]

["Reducing of Negative Energy Balance in Early Lactation Friesian Holstein Cows With The Use of Green Concentrate (Fundamental Research Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)", "2024", "Negative energy balance (NEB) is common in early lactation dairy cows, significantly impacting the performance and metabolism of Friesian Holstein (FH) dairy cows. Feeding green concentrate is an effective strategy to prevent NEB due to its high protein content and palatability. This study aims to assess the effects of green concentrate on the physiological status and metabolic blood profile of dairy cows. Utilizing a completely randomized design (CRD), the study included three treatments with six replications: Commercial Concentrate (CC), Green Concentrate Formulation-1 (GCF1), and Green Concentrate Formulation-2 (GCF2). This research suggests that farmers can utilize green concentrate as an effective measure to mitigate NEB and as a cost-effective substitute for commercial concentrates, ultimately contributing to the improved welfare of dairy farmers."]

["Optimizing Holstein Friesian Calf Performance Through Green Calf Starter Enriched Whey-Dangke Diet (Unhas Internal Grant)", "2024", "Common calf starters often contain fish meal as a primary protein source; however, the strong odor of fish meal is used to hinder calves from consuming the feed, so it needs to be replaced with other protein sources. Hence, this research aims to optimize calf growth performance and nutrient digestibility with whey- dangke enriched green calf starter (fodder-based proteins) in Holstein Friesian. ["Analysis of Corn Quality as Poultry Feed Ingredients Against Indonesian National Standards (SNI) for Feed Quality Control in South Sulawesi", "2024", "Corn is the main component of the feed industry where 50% of corn production in Indonesia is used to meet the needs of the feed industry, while only around 30% is for consumption, and the rest is for other industrial needs. ["Evaluation of Alternative Antioxidants: Fractionation of Cashew Fruit Seed Skin (Annacardium occidentale L.) to Improve Poultry Health In Vitro", "2024", "Livestock exposed to inappropriate environmental conditions, poor feed, and thermal stress can experience various health problems in addition to decreased production and growth disorders, this can also increase the risk of disease, and cause oxidative stress. Oxidative stress can damage cells in the body due to an imbalance between free radical production and the ability of the antioxidant system so that it can cause decreased immune function, affecting livestock growth, production and reproduction. Solutions to overcome the negative effects of oxidative stress can be done by providing feed (proper nutrition), and implementing effective health management practices (use of antioxidants). Antioxidants help fight oxidative stress by neutralizing free radicals that can damage blood cells, and can help prevent damage caused by oxidative reactions. Cashew nut skin is a major by-product of the cashew nut industry whose processing is still rarely done and has many uses in the fields of medicine and industry. Cashew fruit seed coat is reported to have antioxidant properties because the bioactive compounds contained are anacardic acid, cardol, cardanol, and methyl cardol which are natural phenol compounds that can protect blood cells from oxidative damage, by capturing free radicals that can damage cell membranes and can also control the activity of antioxidant enzymes in the blood that help stop the oxidation chain reaction. One way to separate the desired antioxidant compounds is to extract the cashew fruit seed coat using the maceration method with 96% ethanol solvent. The use of ethanol as a solvent in the maceration process has the advantage of dissolving a wider range of compounds including nonpolar or polar compounds and can accelerate the extraction process because of its nature which can dissolve active substances efficiently. Flavonoids and phenols as antioxidants have the ability to quickly provide hydrogen atoms to radical compounds or change them into a more stable form. Flavonoids can provide antioxidant effects by preventing the formation of free radicals, directly capturing free radicals, protecting lipophilic antioxidants and stimulating an increase in enzymatic antioxidants. Antioxidants are compounds that slow down or prevent the oxidation process by stopping the chain reaction of free radicals. Antioxidants are compounds that in certain levels can inhibit or counteract the negative impacts of the oxidation process. Antioxidants control and reduce oxidative damage in feed by delaying or inhibiting oxidation caused by reactive oxygen species, which ultimately increases the shelf life and quality of feed. The previously tested antioxidant products are then given to KUB chickens with parameters of antioxidant blood levels and blood biochemical tests such as glucose levels, cholesterol levels and proteins which aim to evaluate the effects of antioxidant products on the health and performance of KUB chickens. Analysis of the results will help determine whether the administration of antioxidant products has a positive effect on the health of KUB chickens, with the potential to improve the quality and productivity of KUB chicken farms as a whole."]

["Addition of Guanidino Acetic Acid as a Feed Additive to Improve the Performance of Native Chickens", "2023", "The body naturally produces guanidinoacetic acid (GAA), an organic acid that serves as a precursor to creatine, an energy carrier in cells. The native chicken was allotted to 4 treatments, each with 5 replicates of 6 chickens/pen. Four commercial diets were as control (without added GAA and Betaine): 0.06% GAA + 0.1% Betaine, 0.12% GAA + 0.1% Betaine, and 0.18% GAA + 0.1% Betaine. As a result, GAA provides additional energy for optimal growth. The criteria of responses were feed intake, feed efficiency, body weight gains, carcass weight, innards weight and length, intestinal morphology, histology on muscle, and meat quality. Supplementation of native chicken diets with 0.06 GAA resulted in the highest live weight gain, chicken wings, and chicken thighs. In 0.12 GAA, they resulted in the highest average daily gain, lowest feed conversion ratio, carcass weight, breast thighs, chicken back, and chicken lower leg. In 0.18 GAA, the lowest feed intake, feed efficiency, and meat cholesterol were found. Different GAA levels tend to give different results on native chicken performances."]

["Hydroxyapatite (HA) Synthesis from Leg Bone By-Product of Beef Cattle: Structural and Optical Characteristics for Various Sintering Temperatures", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia, 26 February 2024/love-reg/ Bone is one of the by-products of the livestock industry. ["Finding Little Tuna from Space: How Ocean Conditions Reveal Its Best Habitat in the Makassar Strait", "Have you ever imagined that the presence of fish in the ocean could be predicted by reading water temperature, color, and salinity from satellites? A study conducted by Andi Risda Fitrianti Abudarda, Mukti Zainuddin, Rachmat Hidayat, and Siti Khadijah Srioktoviana from Universitas Hasanuddin explored this question through satellite-based habitat modeling. The study, entitled “Habitat modeling of little tuna ( Euthynnus affinis ) in Makassar Strait (Indonesia) using MaxEnt,” was published in Biodiversitas , Volume 27, Issue 1, January 2026."]

["Following the Skipjack Trail: How Satellites Reveal the Hidden Journey of Tuna in Indonesian Waters", "Have we ever wondered what happens when a fish is caught before it has had the chance to reproduce? For skipjack tuna ( Katsuwonus pelamis ), one of the most important pelagic fish species in Indonesian fisheries, this simple question is closely linked to the future of the stock and the livelihoods of coastal communities that depend on the sea. A recent study suggests that the answer can be found by looking at two very different sources of information: the reproductive tissues of fish under a microscope and ocean conditions observed from hundreds of kilometers above the Earth. The study, entitled “Identifying local migration and habitat use of reproductive skipjack tuna ( Katsuwonus pelamis ) in the Bone Bay–Flores Sea, Indonesia,” conducted by Rachmat Hidayat and colleagues, was published in the Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Research , Volume 52, Issue 2, June 2026."]

["From Space to Fishing Grounds: Satellites Reveal Scad Hotspots in Bone Gulf", "A fishing ground may look empty from the surface, but satellites can reveal where the ocean is creating favorable conditions below. The study combined MODIS-AQUA satellite data on sea surface temperature and chlorophyll-a with actual catch locations. These two oceanographic indicators help describe the environmental conditions that influence where scad fish are likely to gather. Sea surface temperature affects fish metabolism and movement, while chlorophyll-a provides an indication of marine productivity and the availability of food at the base of the food web"]

["As the Ocean Changes, Small Pelagic Fish Are Moving Too", "Small pelagic fish such as sardines, anchovies, mackerel, scads, and lemuru may be small in size, but they carry an enormous ecological and economic responsibility. They transfer energy from plankton to larger predators, support coastal fisheries, and contribute to food availability. Yet because many of these species spend much of their lives near the ocean surface, they are especially sensitive to changes in temperature and other environmental conditions. A global review led by researchers from Hasanuddin University examined how climate variability and changing ocean conditions have influenced the distribution of dominant small pelagic fish from 1974 to 2022 . The study brought together findings on European sardines, mackerel, anchovies, Decapterus species, and Sardinella from tropical, subtropical, and temperate waters."]

["Teaching AI to Read the Sea: Neural Networks Reveal Indian Mackerel Hotspots in the Banda Sea", "Finding fish at sea has traditionally depended on experience, weather, and knowledge passed between generations of fishers. ["Small Fish, Big Role: Satellites Reveal How Anchovy Hotspots Move Across the Banda Sea", "A small fish can have a very large role in the ocean. ["Satellite image analysis and seagrass ecosystem characteristics of Palu Bay and changes in seagrass health.", "Seagrass meadows provide a variety of material, non-material and regulatory coastal ecosystem service; however, as the distribution of seagrass beds changes over time due to both anthropogenic activities and natural factors, it is important to monitor changes in seagrass condition. Seagrass meadows in Palu Bay are threatened by activities such as coastal development and land reclamation. Additionally, the bay was hit by a significant tsunami in 2018, which could have impacted ecosystems in the bay, including seagrass meadows. The aim of this study was to detect changes in seagrass extent and distribution over a 10-year period from 2012 to 2022 and changes in land use over approximately a decade (2010 and 2021) through the use of remote sensing technology. Changes in eagrass meadow areal extent were analyzed using data from a 2012 Landsat 7 Satellite Data Acquisition and a 2022 Landsat 8 Satellite Data Acquisition. Water column correction was implemented using the Lyzenga Algorithm. The results showed a significant decrease in the area of seagrass meadows around the coastal area of Palu Bay. Seagrass meadows in 2012 and 2022 covered 127.08 Ha and 87.79 Ha, respectively, indicating a decrease in extent of 43.29 Ha. As the accuracy of the satellite data classification results was 80%, the results are considered acceptable. Anthropogenic activities (mainly mining and construction related) are strongly suspected as the main drivers of this decline, while earthquake and tsunami events likely aggravated the degradation of coastal ecosystems in Palu Bay, including seagrass meadows."]

["SPATIAL MAPPING OF POTENTIAL AREAS FOR LOBSTER CAPTURE AND AQUACULTURE IN SOUTH SULAWESI BASED ON BIOECOLOGICAL ANALYSIS", "Lobster aquaculture represents a strategic opportunity to support marine food self-sufficiency and improve the economic well-being of coastal communities in Indonesia. However, the development of this sector is still hindered by the lack of spatial and bioecological data that could serve as a basis for determining optimal aquaculture sites. In South Sulawesi, the capture of lobster seeds and broodstock by local communities has been ongoing for a long time, but most of this activity remains undocumented and underutilised for scientifically based aquaculture. This study aims to identify potential sites for lobster capture and aquaculture along the coastal areas of South Sulawesi using a bioecological approach and local community participation. The research focuses on three exploratory regions: Tanakeke Island (Takalar Regency), the waters of Jeneponto Regency, and Bulukumba Regency. These areas were selected based on preliminary information from local fishers regarding the presence of lobster seeds and broodstock, as well as habitat characteristics believed to support tropical lobsters from the genus Panulirus , such as P. ornatus , P. homarus , and P. versicolor . The method used is descriptive and exploratory in nature, employing a combination of quantitative and qualitative approaches. The first stage involves collecting spatial information through semi-structured interviews with local fishers to identify capture locations and their habitat characteristics based on Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK). The second stage includes conducting field-based bioecological surveys involving the measurement of environmental parameters such as temperature, salinity, pH, ocean currents, depth, and type of bottom substrate—factors that are crucial in determining the suitability of lobster aquaculture."]

[". Bioecology of banana prawn (Penaeus Merguensis De Man, 1888) based on habitats in the waters of Merauke district, Papua", "The waters of Merauke District have the potential of banana prawn ( Penaeus merguensis De Man, 1888) resources, which have been increasing since the fishing moratorium of 2014. However, the utilization of these resources has not been optimal due to the difficulty in determining the presence of banana prawn. Additionally, research on determining the presence of banana prawn is still limited. Objective : This study aims to analyze the biological aspects of shrimp, feeding habits, density distribution, and determine potential banana prawn fishing areas in the shallow waters of Merauke District. This research was conducted from March 2022 to March 2023. The methods used included prawn size data collection, stomach content analysis, catch, prawn density, oceanographic parameters (temperature, salinity, turbidity, pH, substrate, and mollusk abundance), and coordinate data. Data analysis included length and weight measurements, stomach content analysis, density analysis, and potential fishing area analysis. Result : The research findings indicate that in the biological aspect analysis, the highest size of dominant adult shrimp was found in the mangrove habitat, while in the sandy beach habitat in Payum, mangrove in Yobar, and sandy beach in Lampu Satu, dominant sub-adult were found. Differences are also observed in the estuarine habitat at the mouth of Maro River, where two different sizes, namely juvenile and sub-adult, were dominant. In the analysis of food habits, it was found that the type of food, in the form of mollusks, positively correlates with catch results, thus this finding can be used as one of the variables in predicting potential fishing zones. Meanwhile, in the density analysis, temperature, salinity, turbidity, and abundance of mollusks were proven to significantly influence the density of banana prawns. Additionally, it also indicates that the highest density of banana prawns was found in the mangrove habitat in Bokem, followed by mangrove in Yobar, sandy beach in Payum, and Lampu Satu. The lowest was found in the estuarine habitat at the Maro River. Therefore, in mapping potential capture zones, it is indicated that the mangrove habitat area in Bokem is a potential capture zone because it is supported by the size of dominant adult prawns found in this habitat. Additionally, this area is rich in mollusks with the highest abundance found in this area, where mollusks are the primary food source for banana prawns, especially mature ones. The Bokem mangrove habitat is also supported by high prawn density and optimal oceanographic parameters, thus supporting the presence of banana prawns living within it. Conclusion: Habitat-based capture area studies indicate that mangrove habitats are potential capture areas for banana prawns, supported by increasing mature sizes and high mollusk abundance in this habitat as the primary food source for banana prawns. Additionally, banana prawn abundance is also found to be high in this habitat."]

["Downstreaming of a Smart Water Quality Monitoring System for the Commercialization of Aquaculture Industry Products in Support of a Sustainable Blue Economy", "2025", "The aquaculture sector is a fundamental pillar for Indonesia's food security and blue economy, yet its productivity is often hampered by water quality instability. Fluctuations in vital parameters such as temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen pose a serious threat to the survival of aquatic life, ultimately causing significant losses for farmers. This problem is particularly felt by MSME (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises) hatcheries and small-scale farmers who have limited access to accurate and affordable real-time monitoring technology, creating a technology gap with large-scale industries. To bridge this gap, Aquanotes was developed as a smart water quality monitoring system based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI). This device not only performs automatic data acquisition but also provides predictive analysis and recommendations for preventive actions for farmers. The innovation of Aquanotes lies in its integration of industrial-standard multi-sensors, a compact and portable design, and a rental-based business model specifically designed to address the capital limitations of MSMEs. This product was developed through a user-centered design approach and has resulted in intellectual property in the form of an Industrial Design. The Aquanotes downstreaming project is designed in a two-year strategic roadmap (2025-2026) through collaboration with an industry partner, PT Media Teknologi Celebes. The goal is to increase its Technology Readiness Level (TRL) from TRL 6-7 to TRL 8-9, making it ready for full commercialization. In the first year (2025), the main focus is on Product and Business Model Validation. This phase serves as a crucial foundation before proceeding to the production stage. Three main activities will be carried out: first, prototype validation with a user acceptance target of at least 80% stating the product is beneficial. Second, business model validation to ensure commercial viability, especially by testing the rental scheme through surveys and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs). Third, dissemination of results and formalization of the partnership through the signing of a Cooperation Agreement (PKS). The mandatory output by the end of 2025 is a business model that has been validated and formally agreed upon by the research team and the industry partner. Entering the second year (2026), the program continues to the Downstreaming and Full Commercialization stage. Based on the validated model, activities will begin with design finalization and pilot-scale production for standardization. The pilot products will then undergo industry feasibility testing and certification processes to meet market standards. In parallel, the business plan will be finalized into a binding commercialization agreement. Intellectual Property protection is also a priority, with the target of obtaining 'granted' status for the registered Industrial Design. The mandatory output by the end of 2026 is an Aquanotes product that is tested, certified, and legally protected, marking its readiness for a broad market launch and to make a tangible contribution to the sustainable blue economy in Indonesia."]

["Unlocking Rural Competitiveness: How Village Enterprises Turn Grassroots Skills into Lasting Market Power", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 8 September 2026/FSRAG/ – Rural economies form the true bedrock of national development, driving community self-reliance and creating vital local livelihoods . Under Indonesia's national agenda to build the country from its periphery, Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) alongside Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have emerged as essential catalysts for grassroots growth . Yet, rural businesses often face intense market challenges, particularly when operating near major multinational industrial zones . Unlike large corporations that rely on vast economies of scale, rural small enterprises must discover unique sources of competitive advantage to survive, grow, and secure consistent market share . A foundational empirical study authored by Cepi Pahlevi, Otto Randa Payangan, Sabir, and Andi Harmoko Arifin explores these grassroots business mechanics . The research, titled \"Competitive Advantages of Small Scale Enterprises (UMKM) and Village Owned Enterprises (BUMDES) as a Central Development Area (NAWACITA) in Luwu Timur District,\" was published in the Journal of Advanced Research in Dynamical and Control Systems (JARDCS) (Vol. 12, Issue 13, pp. 635–645, ISSN: 1943-023X, DOI: 10.5373/JARDCS/V1213/20201927) by publisher Institute of Advanced Scientific Research on February 27, 2020 . Investigating 80 rural enterprise managers and BUMDes directors across Luwu Timur Regency, South Sulawesi, the authors examined how positional advantages and internal resource competencies collectively drive firm performance . The empirical findings reveal a vital strategic lesson: superficial corporate structures alone cannot guarantee business success for rural enterprises . Formalities like share-based ownership or external capital grants from municipal authorities often showed negligible direct effects on business growth due to bureaucratic delays and access barriers . Instead, sustainable enterprise performance is driven by internal sources of advantage, specifically managerial skill sets and agile resource utilization . Capabilities such as conservative cost control, product innovation, niche market focus, responsive customer service, and reliable product quality directly transform operating positions into superior sales and expanding market reach ( $R^2 = 0.848$ , $F = 28.295$ , $p = 0.000$ ) . When rural enterprises combine practical organizational skills with focused market positioning, the interaction significantly accelerates business performance . ["Why Good Governance Matters More Than Financial Ratios Alone", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 3 July 2026/FSRAG/ – A company can have plenty of cash, manageable debt, and strong financial resources, but does that automatically make it valuable in the eyes of investors? Not necessarily. For manufacturing companies, creating lasting value depends not only on financial strength but also on how effectively managers use company resources and how well corporate governance protects shareholder interests. A study by Meliyanti, Cepi Pahlevi, and Fauzi R. Rahim explores this issue in Indonesia’s manufacturing sector. The research, titled “The Influence of Current Ratio (CR), Return On Investment (ROI), Debt To Equity Ratio (DER) on Company Value with Good Corporate Governance as a Moderating Variable (Case Study of Manufacturing Companies Listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange for the 2016–2020 Period),” was published in Jurnal Penelitian Ekonomi dan Akuntansi (JPENSI), Volume 9, Number 1, pages 14–25 , by Universitas Islam Lamongan on February 10, 2024 . The researchers used Moderated Regression Analysis to examine manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2016–2020. They focused on three financial indicators: Current Ratio (CR), Return on Investment (ROI), and Debt to Equity Ratio (DER). Company value was measured using Price to Book Value (PBV), while managerial share ownership was used to represent Good Corporate Governance. The results reveal a clear message for investors and business leaders: profitability matters . Return on Investment had a positive and statistically significant effect on company value, with p = 0.001 and t = 3.764. This means companies that use their resources effectively to generate returns are more likely to be viewed positively by investors. Interestingly, the Current Ratio and Debt to Equity Ratio did not have significant direct effects on company value. In other words, simply having large amounts of liquid assets or maintaining a particular debt level does not automatically make a company more valuable. What matters is how those resources are managed and transformed into productive business activities and sustainable profits. This is where Good Corporate Governance becomes important. When managers own shares in the company, their interests may become more closely aligned with those of shareholders. This can encourage managers to use resources carefully, control unnecessary risks, and make decisions that support long-term company performance. The findings are closely connected to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17): Partnerships for the Goals . Strong corporate governance requires trust, accountability, transparency, and cooperation among managers, shareholders, investors, regulators, and other stakeholders. These relationships can help companies make more responsible financial decisions and build sustainable businesses. Ultimately, financial ratios are only part of the story. A healthy balance sheet does not guarantee strong company value if resources are poorly managed. For Indonesia’s manufacturing sector, the combination of profitability, responsible financial management, and effective governance can create stronger investor confidence and more resilient businesses. The lesson is simple: financial resources create potential, but good management and good governance turn that potential into lasting value. Doi: Doi: 10.30736/.v9i1.1854 Contact Info Name : Prof . Cepi Pahlevi, S.E., M.Si Phone/Mobile : +62 813-4193-6368 Email : cepipahlevi@fe.unhas.ac.id"]

["Smart Banking Needs Smart Customers: Why Digital Literacy Matters", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 12 April 2026/FSRAG/ – Smart Banking Needs Smart Customers: Why Digital Literacy Matters Banking is becoming faster, easier, and increasingly digital. Rahim explores how financial and digital literacy influence people’s readiness to use smart banking services. Meanwhile, digital literacy allows customers to interact more comfortably with automated banking systems. People with stronger digital skills may be more willing to explore self-service facilities, while those unfamiliar with digital interfaces may feel hesitant or even avoid them. They can also become learning spaces where customers gradually develop confidence in using digital financial services. With appropriate guidance and support, customers who once depended heavily on conventional banking counters may eventually become more independent digital banking users. ["From ESG Rules to Business Strength: Why Risk Management Matters", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 22 Agustus 2026/FSRAG/ – From ESG Rules to Business Strength: Why Risk Management Matters Mining and energy companies are among the most important contributors to economic development, but they also face serious environmental and social challenges. The study, titled “When Risk Management and Regulation Shape ESG Performance Links in Indonesian Mining and Energy,” was published in the proceedings Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research, Volume 388, pages 258–273 , by Atlantis Press, part of Springer Nature , in 2026 . The article has the DOI 10.2991/978-94-6239-709-5-19 . The researchers analyzed responses from 143 executives representing 50 publicly listed mining and energy companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) . The findings provide an important lesson for businesses: ESG can create greater value when it becomes part of everyday risk management rather than simply a compliance requirement . Consider a mining company facing stricter environmental regulations, community concerns, or climate-related risks. If these issues are treated as separate sustainability problems, the company may react only after damage has occurred. But when environmental and social risks are included in the company’s risk-management system, managers can identify potential problems earlier and prepare better responses. The study found that Risk Management Effectiveness (RME) plays a key mediating role between ESG orientation and financial performance. In simple terms, ESG practices can contribute to better financial outcomes when companies know how to identify, assess, and manage the risks associated with sustainability. Regulation also matters. Stronger regulatory pressure can reinforce the relationship between effective risk management and financial performance. Instead of seeing regulations as burdens, companies can use them as incentives to improve governance, strengthen internal systems, and prepare for future risks. These findings are closely connected to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17): Partnerships for the Goals , particularly Targets 17.14 and 17.16. Sustainable development requires cooperation among governments, companies, investors, financial institutions, researchers, and communities. Strong partnerships can help transform sustainability policies into practical business strategies. For Indonesia’s mining and energy sector, the message is clear: sustainability should not stop at producing ESG reports. Companies need to integrate environmental and social considerations into their strategic decisions and risk-management systems. Ultimately, ESG is not only about protecting the environment or satisfying regulators. It can also be a tool for building stronger, more resilient businesses . Companies that combine sustainability, effective risk management, and collaboration may be better prepared for regulatory change, environmental uncertainty, and growing stakeholder expectations."]

["More Debt Does Not Always Mean More Value: What Really Matters for Food and Beverage Companies?", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 22 June 2026/FSRAG/ – Every day, people buy food and drinks without thinking much about the companies behind these products. The food and beverage industry is one of the more resilient parts of the economy because demand for essential consumer products can remain relatively stable even when economic conditions become uncertain. But for these companies, an important question remains: does taking on more debt or increasing operating leverage actually make a company more valuable? A study by Sun Dewi Putri, Cepi Pahlevi, and Fauzi R. Rahim provides an interesting answer. The research, titled “Effect of Operating Leverage and Financial Leverage on Firm Value through Financial Performance,” was published in Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research, Volume 331, pages 1130–1148 , by Atlantis Press, part of Springer Nature , on July 30, 2025 . The article’s DOI is 10.2991/978-94-6463-758-8_92 . The researchers examined 34 food and beverage companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) using 170 audited financial reports covering 2019–2023. They focused on two types of leverage: operating leverage , which relates to how fixed operating costs affect business performance, and financial leverage , which reflects the use of debt to finance a company. They also examined financial performance through Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE). The most interesting finding is that profitability matters more than leverage alone . Financial performance had a positive and statistically significant effect on firm value, with p = 0.009 and t = 2.630. This means companies that can efficiently use their assets and generate sustainable profits are more likely to receive positive attention from investors. However, operating leverage and financial leverage did not have significant direct effects on financial performance or firm value. Financial performance also did not significantly mediate the relationship between leverage and firm value. What does this mean in everyday business terms? Simply having more debt does not automatically make a company more valuable. Borrowing can provide additional capital, but if that money does not generate stronger profits, investors may see little reason to increase the company’s valuation. For food and beverage companies, the lesson is particularly important. Rather than focusing excessively on increasing debt, managers should concentrate on using assets efficiently, controlling operating costs, protecting profit margins, and generating consistent returns . These findings are also relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17): Partnerships for the Goals , particularly Targets 17.16 and 17.17. Strong financial governance depends on cooperation and transparent communication among companies, investors, financial institutions, regulators, and other stakeholders. Reliable financial information helps these groups make better decisions and build greater trust. Ultimately, the study offers a simple message: leverage may provide financial power, but profitability creates value . For Indonesia’s food and beverage industry, sustainable earnings, efficient operations, responsible financial management, and transparent governance may be more important for long-term success than simply taking on more debt."]

["In Industry 5.0, Smart Spending Could Be the Key to Higher Profits", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia 30 June 2026/FSRAG/ – The financial services industry is entering a new era. Technology can help companies determine which customers are more likely to respond to specific offers, allowing acquisition budgets to be directed toward opportunities with greater potential returns. Interestingly, COF, OPEX, and NCL did not show statistically significant individual effects on net profit in the study. This suggests that financial costs should not necessarily be viewed in isolation. Their impact depends on how they interact with revenue generation, customer acquisition, operational strategies, and broader business decisions. The findings are also relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17): Partnerships for the Goals , particularly Targets 17.16 and 17.17. Building smarter financial systems requires cooperation among financing companies, technology providers, regulators, researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders. ["From Small Shops to Smart Businesses: How Digital Accounting is Transforming Indonesia’s MSMEs", "In Indonesia, 4 March 2026/APM, small businesses are quietly undergoing a powerful transformation. This shift is not just about technology—it is about opportunity, resilience, and smarter decision-making. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have long been the backbone of Indonesia’s economy. Yet, many of them traditionally relied on manual bookkeeping, which often led to errors, limited financial insight, and slow decision-making. Today, digital accounting is stepping in as a game changer. By using simple software and mobile applications, business owners can now track income, expenses, and profits in real time."]

["Why Responsibility Accounting Matters for a Better Future: Strengthening Governance Through Transparency", "In Indonesia, where public trust in institutions continues to evolve, the need for transparent and accountable governance has become more urgent than ever. Organizations both public and private are increasingly expected to demonstrate not only financial performance but also ethical responsibility. One approach that is gaining attention in this context is responsibility accounting, a system that aligns organizational performance with accountability at every managerial level. Responsibility accounting is not just about tracking numbers; it is about ensuring that every decision-maker is answerable for the outcomes under their control. By clearly defining roles, responsibilities, and performance indicators, organizations can create a culture of transparency and integrity. This is particularly important in supporting Good Corporate Governance (GCG), which emphasizes fairness, accountability, transparency, and responsibility as its core principles."]

["Smart Systems Need Smart People: The Hidden Key to Transparent Government Finance", "South Sulawesi, Indonesia, on August 1, 2025, APM marks the publication of a study titled Human Competencies: Amplifying Financial Reporting Quality in Indonesian Local Government in the Journal of Risk and Financial Management by MDPI (Volume 18, Issue 424) . ["Endogenous Motivation as Perception of Individual Autonomy Expanding the Determinants of Intention to Adopt Digital Accounting", "Research Project receives a grant from the Indonesian Ministry of Research, Technology and Higher Education - National Competitive Research Scheme ( Implementation of Activities in 2024) The objective of this study is to examine and analyze the factors that affect the intention to adopt digital accounting among MSMEs in South Sulawesi Province. ["STUDY OF THE SUSTAINABILITY MODEL OF INTENT TO USE DIGITAL PAYMENTS IN MSMES IN SOUTH SULAWESI", "Research Project receives a Grant from Hasanuddin University - COLLABORATIVE FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH Scheme for 2023 Implementation of Activities in 2023 Our research answers the adaptation behavior of accountants in facing the challenges of the society 5.0 era. ["Study of The Sustainability Model of Intent to Use Digital Payments In SMEs In South Sulawesi", "Research Project receives a Grant from Hasanuddin University - COLLABORATIVE FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH Scheme for 2023 Implementation of Activities in 2023 Our research aims to investigate, identify, and test the most important factors that can influence the continuation of MSME\\'s intention to use QRIS as a digital transaction tool by building multidimensional models, namely TAM and TTF. ["Analysis of local government budget behavior in South Sulawesi", "Research Project receives a grant from The Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology - Implementation of Activities in 2021 (2-Year Research Period) Our research analyzes the behavior of individual budget compilers towards determining the budget amount for the coming period and relates to overreliance on past information and the behavior of budget compilers in overreacting or underreacting to current PAD information that is the same as last year\\'s information or current information that has changed. ["QRIS and MSME Transformation: Towards an Era of Inclusive Digital Payments", "QRIS, developed by Bank Indonesia (BI), aims to realize financial digitalization in response to the demands of the Industrial Revolution 5.0, which emphasizes the interplay between humans and machines. This study investigates, identifies, and tests the key factors influencing MSMEs\\' continued intention to use QRIS as a digital transaction tool by developing a multidimensional model incorporating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) framework. The findings suggest that MSME users can gain enhanced experiences from using technology and technology services, specifically QRIS, more easily. The ubiquitous nature of mobile banking allows customers to access a wide range of banking services quickly, securely, and conveniently, reflecting positively on both the perceived usefulness of the technology and the quality of its functions."]

["Digital Accounting Adoption Model to Achieve National Financial Inclusion Target", "The evolution of technology and the proliferation of smartphone users is changing the way people access financial management services. Bank Indonesia as a financial management service provider in the form of SiApik digital accounting consistently innovates in developing products and services tailored for users to improve the financial performance of MSMEs, thereby achieving Indonesia\\'s national financial inclusion target of 90 percent by 2024. We identify important factors that can influence the continued intention of MSMEs to use the SiApik application to realize financial inclusion. This research develops a technology acceptance model that is widely used today, namely the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), UTAUT has been identified as the most comprehensive model in overcoming the limitations of technology acceptance models. The results showed that the factors that influence MSME actors to adopt digital accounting, namely the SiApik application, are digital financial literacy, digital benefits and perceived ease of use of digital. This study is expected to provide recommendations to the government, especially Bank Indonesia as a service provider and responsible for the national financial inclusion target. This research makes a new contribution by extending the Digital Technology Acceptance Model (DTAM) to include digital financial literacy (DFL) as an important factor influencing the adoption of digital accounting (SiApik) in MSMEs. This research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital literacy impacts financial inclusion in developing countries."]

["The Influence of Leadership Style, Organizational Culture, Organizational Commitment, and Job Satisfaction Through Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB) on the Performance of Public High School Teachers in South Sulawesi", "This study aims to analyze the influence of Organizational Culture, Organizational Commitment, and Job Satisfaction on the performance of public high school teachers in South Sulawesi, with Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB) as an intervening variable. This research employs quantitative analysis using SEM PLS 3.0 with SPSS version 22. The research subjects are teachers in public schools located in South Sulawesi. ["The Impact of Industrial Policy, Structural Transformation, and Economic Growth on Strategic Competitiveness Through Dynamic Capabilities in Industrial Areas: An Empirical Investigation", "This study examines the impact of structural transformation on economic growth in industrial regions of Indonesia and explores the moderating role of dynamic capabilities, particularly through human capital quality and technological innovation. Structural transformation, characterized by a shift from traditional sectors such as agriculture to more productive sectors like manufacturing and services, is crucial for long-term economic development. However, Indonesia faces challenges such as premature deindustrialization, where the contribution of the industrial sector to GDP declines before reaching advanced economic maturity. Using a fixed effects panel data model, this research assesses the relationship between structural transformation and economic growth, including interactions to test whether dynamic capabilities can enhance this relationship. The findings reveal that while structural transformation alone does not significantly drive economic growth, dynamic capabilities such as human capital quality and innovation capacity play an important role in maximizing its benefits. However, the expected positive moderating effects of dynamic capabilities are not fully realized, indicating that policies targeting workforce skills, technological innovation, and infrastructure improvement are still needed."]

["the impact of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) on competitive advantage, environmental performance, and the performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs).", "This research investigates the impact of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) on competitive advantage, environmental performance, and the performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). The findings indicate that GSCM has a significant positive effect on competitive advantage, which in turn significantly enhances both environmental performance and SME performance. However, the direct effects of GSCM on environmental performance and SME performance are not significant. Competitive advantage is found to be a full mediator in the relationship between GSCM and SME performance, while environmental performance does not mediate this relationship. These findings underscore the importance of competitive advantage as a key factor in driving SME performance through the implementation of GSCM."]

["Marketing Research: Strategies for Enhancing Brand Equity of Bank Sulselbar", "The objective of this study is to determine the most important brand attributes of Bank Sulselbar for its customers. ["STRATEGY OF GREEN MARKETING AND GREEN PRODUCT TO IMPROVE ENVIRONMENTALLY-FRIENDLY SMEs’ PERFORMANCE (A STUDY ON SMEs IN SOUTH SULAWESI)", "Strategy of green marketing and green product has an important role in improving the marketing performance of SMEs. The specific objectives of the study are (1) to analyze the effect of green marketing on green product of SMEs in South Sulawesi, (2) to analyze the effect of green marketing on marketing performance of SMEs in South Sulawesi, (3) to analyze the effect of green products on marketing performance of SMEs in South Sulawesi, and (4) design of marketing performance development model through green marketing and green product of SMEs in South Sulawesi. The population was all SMEs registered at the Department of Cooperatives and SMEs in Makassar and Pare-Pare. The sample is SME entrepreneurs who are selected according to the research objectives and meet certain criteria (Purposive Sampling). The respondents were micro and small business actors/entrepreneurs who were selected to represent their businesses with a total of 100 people. Descriptive analysis and Structural Equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS tools were used to solve research problems. The results show that the implementation of green marketing and green products on marketing performance of SMEs in South Sulawesi has a positive and significant effect. This research shows that green product is most important variable in supporting marketing performance. Thus, green product as an intervening variable is very effective in improving the marketing performance of SMEs in South Sulawesi"]

["Model and Strategy for Enhancing Competitiveness and Company Performance through Supply Chain Management Practices, Total Quality Management Practices, and Quality Culture Internalization: A Case Study of the Manufacturing Industry in South Sulawesi", "This study proposes a comprehensive model and strategy to improve the competitiveness and performance of manufacturing companies in South Sulawesi by integrating Supply Chain Management (SCM) practices, Total Quality Management (TQM) practices, and the internalization of a quality-oriented culture. ["Carbon emission disclosure, green innovation, labour practices and decent work on the cost of equity: the role of good corporate governance as a moderating variable", "This research was designed to examine the effect of carbon emission disclosure (CED), green innovation (GI), and labor practices and decent work (LA) on the cost of equity (COE) with good corporate governance (GCG) as a moderating variable. ["Uncovering A Green Footprint: Building A Waste Accounting System For Energy Companies In Eastern Region Of Indonesian", "This is a research plan that is being worked on with doctoral program students. ["The Role Of Sdgs Disclosure On The Effect Of Green Innovation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions, And Ecoefficiency On Firm Value", "This research aims to determine the role of SDGs disclosure on the effect of green innovation, GHG emissions, and eco-efficiency on firm value. The sample were selected through purposive sampling technique. There were 16 companies selected with a total of five years of research, so the total observations in this study were 80 observations. This study used secondary data obtained from the internet through the official IDX website(www.idx.co.id), the website of Yayasan Keanekaragaman Hayati Indonesia (www.kehati.or.id), and the official website of each company. The results of this study show that green innovation and GHG emissions partially affect firm value. An increase in green innovation increases firm value, while an increase in GHG emission affects a decrease in firm value. Meanwhile, eco-efficiency has no significant effect on firm value. ["Integration Of Material Flow Cost Accounting And Resource Efficiency Into Green Accounting: A Strategy For Company Sustainability", "The hypothesis testing results indicate that both green accounting and MFCA positively impact corporate sustainability. ["Exploring the Diverse Consequences of Abusive Supervision on Work Engagement Components: The Impact of Job Insecurity and the Cognitive Demand of Flexible Work", "Makassar, 2026 — Dr. Hillman Wirawan and his research team from Universitas Hasanuddin are currently developing a research project focusing on the evaluation of abusive supervisory behaviors in a cross-cultural context. The project, entitled “Evaluating Abusive Supervisory Behaviors Across Cultures: A Rasch Comparison of Indonesian and Western Samples,” aims to examine how supervisory behaviors perceived as abusive are interpreted by individuals from different cultural backgrounds. This study is particularly important because most theories and measurement instruments related to abusive supervision have been developed in Western countries, while their applicability in Asian cultural settings, including Indonesia, still requires further investigation. In today’s increasingly interconnected global workplace, multinational organizations face challenges in understanding how cultural differences shape employees’ perceptions of leadership behaviors. Actions considered inappropriate or harmful in one culture may not necessarily be perceived in the same way by individuals from another cultural background. Therefore, this study employs the Rasch Measurement Model to compare the measurement characteristics of abusive supervision items across Indonesian and Western samples. This approach enables researchers to determine whether the instrument demonstrates equivalent levels of validity and reliability across different cultural groups. The expected outcome of this research is the provision of empirical evidence regarding measurement equivalence in abusive supervision scales across cultures. Such findings can assist academics and practitioners in developing more accurate instruments for assessing negative leadership behaviors in diverse organizational contexts. Furthermore, the study is expected to contribute to the advancement of global leadership theories by promoting a more inclusive and culturally sensitive understanding of leadership dynamics. From a sustainable development perspective, this research is closely aligned with SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) through its efforts to foster healthier and more productive work environments, as well as SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) by supporting the development of ethical, fair, and accountable leadership practices within modern organizations."]

["IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF IKAT WEAVING IN BUILDING ORGANIZATIONAL CULTURE AND COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE OF SENGKANG WEAVING UMKM", "This study aims to identify the main themes in building the concept of quality in weaving micro/small/medium enterprises (MSMEs ). Using the systematic literature review method and Theo Van Leeuwen\\'s social semiotic theory, this study interprets the meaning of traditional weaving based on the region of origin, interpretation of sign readers, and exchange of meaning through semiotic resources. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with weavers and other stakeholders. The results of the study indicate that quality in weaving MSMEs can be interpreted as: Commitment to continual process improvement, Honesty and respect for culture and nature, Reputation, Investment in human resources (HR),Synergy, and Compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOP). The Total Quality Management (TQM) approach is considered less effective for weaving MSMEs due to the simplicity of their governance. However, the quality aspect remains closely related to HR, production, and management. In addition, mastery of information technology by MSME managers can strengthen the meaning of quality in organizational culture, improve performance, and encourage sustainable competitive advantage."]
