["Unveiling the potential of generative artificial intelligence: a multidimensional journey into the future", "Perkembangan kecerdasan buatan generatif (Generative Artificial Intelligence atau GenAI) serta peluang penerapannya dalam berbagai aspek kehidupan. Artikel yang diterbitkan dalam Industrial Management & Data Systems ini melihat GenAI bukan sekadar sebagai inovasi teknologi, tetapi sebagai perkembangan yang dapat memengaruhi berbagai sektor, seperti pendidikan, bisnis, industri, komunikasi, pariwisata, dan perhotelan. GenAI memiliki kemampuan untuk menciptakan berbagai bentuk konten baru berdasarkan data dan pola yang telah dipelajarinya. Konten tersebut dapat berupa tulisan, gambar, suara, video, hingga kode pemrograman. Kemampuan tersebut menjadi salah satu pembeda penting antara GenAI dan penggunaan AI sebelumnya yang lebih banyak diarahkan untuk pengolahan data, analisis, serta prediksi. Dengan adanya GenAI, teknologi mulai memiliki peran yang lebih luas dalam membantu manusia mengembangkan gagasan dan menghasilkan berbagai bentuk karya. Ooi dan rekan-rekannya melihat perkembangan GenAI dari berbagai sudut pandang. Dalam sektor bisnis, teknologi ini dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mendukung produktivitas, membantu pekerjaan administratif, mengembangkan strategi pemasaran, serta memahami kebutuhan konsumen. Sementara dalam bidang pendidikan, GenAI dapat digunakan sebagai sarana pendukung proses belajar dan penelitian. Meskipun demikian, pemanfaatannya tetap membutuhkan kontrol manusia karena informasi yang diberikan oleh AI tidak selalu benar, dan sistem tersebut dapat menghasilkan jawaban yang mengandung kesalahan atau bias. Potensi yang sama juga terlihat dalam industri pariwisata dan perhotelan. GenAI dapat dimanfaatkan untuk membuat materi promosi destinasi, menyediakan informasi bagi wisatawan, memberikan rekomendasi perjalanan, dan menciptakan layanan yang lebih sesuai dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Kemampuan teknologi dalam menghasilkan konten dengan cepat juga dapat membantu pengelola destinasi memperkenalkan daya tarik wisata, termasuk kekayaan budaya dan berbagai produk pariwisata, melalui media digital. Dengan demikian, GenAI dapat menjadi salah satu pendukung strategi pemasaran dan pengembangan daya saing destinasi wisata. Di balik berbagai manfaat tersebut, penggunaan GenAI juga menimbulkan sejumlah tantangan. Persoalan seperti perlindungan data pribadi, keamanan informasi, hak cipta, bias algoritma, keakuratan informasi, serta penyalahgunaan teknologi perlu mendapatkan perhatian. Oleh karena itu, penerapan GenAI tidak dapat hanya berfokus pada kecanggihan dan efisiensi teknologi. Aspek etika, tanggung jawab, serta peran manusia tetap diperlukan untuk memastikan bahwa teknologi digunakan secara tepat. Secara keseluruhan, artikel ini menunjukkan bahwa GenAI memiliki potensi besar untuk membawa perubahan dalam berbagai bidang. Perkembangan teknologi tersebut dapat menciptakan peluang baru sekaligus menghadirkan tantangan yang perlu dikelola. Pemanfaatan GenAI yang efektif membutuhkan keseimbangan antara inovasi teknologi, kebutuhan manusia, pertimbangan etis, dan pengawasan yang memadai. Dengan pendekatan tersebut, GenAI dapat diarahkan menjadi teknologi yang memberikan manfaat bagi masyarakat dan mendukung perkembangan berbagai sektor pada masa mendatang."]

["Heritage tourism and regional growth: New insights and implications from spatial analysis", "Mengkaji keterkaitan antara pariwisata warisan budaya dan perkembangan ekonomi di tingkat regional. Kajian ini menempatkan heritage tourism tidak hanya sebagai aktivitas yang berkaitan dengan kunjungan ke situs sejarah, museum, galeri, maupun bangunan bersejarah, tetapi juga sebagai kegiatan yang berpotensi memberikan kontribusi terhadap pertumbuhan suatu daerah. Penelitian tersebut secara khusus melihat apakah manfaat yang muncul dari kegiatan pariwisata hanya dirasakan oleh daerah yang memiliki objek wisata atau turut menyebar ke wilayah yang berada di sekitarnya. Penelitian dilakukan dengan menggunakan data regional di Inggris serta pendekatan analisis spasial. Salah satu metode yang digunakan adalah Spatial Durbin Model (SDM), yang digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi keterkaitan antara suatu wilayah dengan wilayah lain di sekitarnya. Pendekatan ini menjadi penting karena aktivitas pariwisata pada dasarnya tidak selalu terbatas pada wilayah administratif tertentu. Peningkatan jumlah wisatawan pada sebuah destinasi dapat mendorong perkembangan berbagai kegiatan ekonomi, seperti usaha penginapan, transportasi, perdagangan, kuliner, serta sektor jasa lainnya. Kondisi tersebut memungkinkan manfaat pariwisata menyebar ke kawasan yang berdekatan dengan destinasi utama. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan adanya hubungan positif antara kunjungan ke objek warisan budaya dan pertumbuhan ekonomi regional. Meskipun demikian, pengaruh yang dihasilkan ternyata berbeda berdasarkan jenis objek heritage yang dikunjungi. Museum dan galeri seni menunjukkan adanya dampak ekonomi yang tidak hanya dirasakan di lokasi objek tersebut, tetapi juga dapat memberikan manfaat kepada wilayah di sekitarnya. Fenomena ini dikenal sebagai spillover effect. Keberadaan fasilitas budaya tersebut dapat meningkatkan mobilitas wisatawan sekaligus mendorong munculnya aktivitas ekonomi pendukung di kawasan lain. Berbeda dengan museum dan galeri seni, properti atau bangunan bersejarah cenderung memberikan pengaruh ekonomi yang lebih besar pada wilayah tempat objek tersebut berada. Perbedaan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa karakteristik masing-masing objek warisan budaya perlu menjadi pertimbangan dalam merancang strategi pengembangan pariwisata. Setiap jenis heritage memiliki kemampuan dan pola yang berbeda dalam menghasilkan manfaat ekonomi. Hasil penelitian juga menunjukkan bahwa pengembangan pariwisata warisan budaya perlu dikaitkan dengan perencanaan pembangunan wilayah. Pengelolaan destinasi tidak cukup hanya berfokus pada objek utama, tetapi juga perlu mempertimbangkan aksesibilitas, infrastruktur, fasilitas pendukung, serta keterlibatan masyarakat di kawasan sekitarnya. Dengan pendekatan tersebut, manfaat ekonomi dari heritage tourism dapat menjangkau masyarakat yang lebih luas. Dalam konteks arkeologi pariwisata, kajian ini dapat menjadi rujukan untuk melihat situs arkeologi dari perspektif yang lebih luas. Situs tidak hanya dipahami sebagai peninggalan masa lalu yang perlu dilestarikan, tetapi juga dapat menjadi bagian dari pengembangan wilayah apabila dikelola secara tepat. Analisis spasial dapat membantu melihat hubungan antara lokasi situs, pola kunjungan wisatawan, fasilitas pariwisata, dan aktivitas ekonomi masyarakat. Dengan demikian, pemanfaatan warisan budaya dapat diarahkan untuk mendukung perkembangan ekonomi dan sosial tanpa mengabaikan prinsip pelestarian nilai budaya."]

["NARASI BUDAYA DALAM LANSKAP PARIWISATA BERKELANJUTAN : STUDI KASUS KAWASAN GEOPARK MAROS PANGKEP", "Membahas tentang keterkaitan antara unsur budaya masyarakat dengan upaya pengembangan pariwisata yang berkelanjutan di kawasan Geopark Maros Pangkep. Kawasan ini memiliki bentang alam karst yang menjadi salah satu kekayaan alam penting di Sulawesi Selatan. Meskipun demikian, potensi kawasan tersebut tidak hanya terbatas pada kondisi geologi dan panorama alamnya. Berbagai peninggalan sejarah, tradisi, pengetahuan lokal, serta aktivitas masyarakat juga menjadi bagian yang tidak terpisahkan dari karakter dan identitas kawasan. Dalam pengembangan destinasi wisata, unsur budaya dapat digunakan untuk memberikan gambaran yang lebih lengkap mengenai suatu tempat. Sebuah kawasan pada dasarnya tidak hanya memiliki objek untuk dilihat, tetapi juga menyimpan berbagai cerita yang berkembang dari kehidupan masyarakatnya. Kisah mengenai asal-usul tempat, tradisi yang diwariskan dari generasi ke generasi, cara masyarakat memanfaatkan lingkungan, serta keberadaan peninggalan budaya dapat menjadi materi yang menarik untuk disampaikan kepada wisatawan. Oleh karena itu, pengembangan Geopark Maros Pangkep sebaiknya tidak hanya berfokus pada keindahan kawasan karst, tetapi juga memperhatikan kehidupan budaya yang berkembang di sekitarnya. Narasi budaya dapat berperan sebagai sarana untuk menjelaskan nilai dan makna yang terdapat di balik suatu objek wisata. Melalui narasi tersebut, wisatawan dapat mengetahui alasan suatu tempat, benda, atau tradisi memiliki arti penting bagi masyarakat. Gua, situs arkeologi, kawasan permukiman, maupun berbagai tradisi lokal, misalnya, dapat diperkenalkan dengan menghubungkannya pada sejarah dan pengalaman masyarakat. Cara penyampaian seperti ini dapat membuat kegiatan wisata tidak sekadar menjadi aktivitas melihat objek, tetapi juga menjadi pengalaman untuk memahami latar belakang budaya suatu kawasan. Aspek keberlanjutan menjadi hal yang tidak kalah penting dalam pengembangan pariwisata di kawasan geopark. Pengelolaan wisata seharusnya tidak hanya berorientasi pada peningkatan jumlah wisatawan dan manfaat ekonomi, tetapi juga memperhatikan kondisi lingkungan serta kepentingan masyarakat setempat. Keterlibatan tersebut juga dapat membantu menjaga agar cerita dan informasi budaya yang disampaikan kepada wisatawan tetap sesuai dengan kondisi serta nilai yang berlaku di masyarakat. Geopark Maros Pangkep mempunyai peluang untuk mengembangkan konsep wisata yang memadukan kekayaan alam dengan warisan budaya. Dengan pendekatan tersebut, pengalaman wisatawan tidak hanya berfokus pada pemandangan alam, tetapi juga memberikan kesempatan untuk mengenal sejarah, kehidupan, dan kebudayaan masyarakat di kawasan geopark. Pada akhirnya, narasi budaya dapat menjadi salah satu unsur penting dalam membangun identitas sebuah destinasi wisata. Penyampaian cerita yang didasarkan pada sejarah, lingkungan, dan pengalaman masyarakat lokal dapat membantu memperkenalkan karakter Geopark Maros Pangkep secara lebih menyeluruh. Pendekatan ini juga dapat mendukung pengembangan pariwisata yang tetap memperhatikan kelestarian lingkungan dan keberadaan budaya lokal. ["COMMUNITY BASED APPROACH (COMMUNITY BASED APPROACH) AS POST PANDEMIC TOURISM RESILIENCE", "This research, funded under the 2022 National Competitive Research Grant, explores the role of a Community-Based Approach (CBA) in fostering resilience within the tourism sector in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. ["Exploring Middle Holocene Burial and Cultural Dynamics at Liang Sumpang Karoro 1, Maros, Indonesia", "The research focuses on archaeological discoveries at Liang Sumpang Karoro 1, a cave site in Maros Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. ["Analysis and Prediction of Significant Meteorological (SIGMET) in the Eastern Indonesia Aviation Region", "Muhlis, Sandi, Anita Ramadhani, Halmar Halide ABSTRACT The spatial and temporal distribution of Significant Meteorological Information (SIGMET) in Eastern Indonesia reflects the complex dynamics of geographical and meteorological interactions that influence the formation of extreme weather. This study highlights the SIGMET distribution pattern from 2019 to 2022, focusing on the regions of Papua, Southeast Sulawesi, and South Kalimantan. SIGMET is identified as an important indicator in mitigating aviation risks, especially related to thunderstorms, convective clouds, and turbulence. Spatially, Papua is the region with the highest SIGMET activity, supported by high mountainous topography that creates a local convergence zone. Southeast Sulawesi shows a significant SIGMET pattern, especially around Bone Bay, due to the interaction of the southwest monsoon wind with complex topography. South Kalimantan, despite its relatively flat topography, still records SIGMET activity due to the influence of airflow from the Java Sea. Temporally, SIGMET is more active during the rainy season (October-March), when the west monsoon wind brings water vapor from the Indian Ocean, creating ideal conditions for the formation of convective clouds. In contrast, activity decreases during the dry season (April-September), except in certain areas such as Papua which continue to record SIGMET sporadically. The transition season, both from rainy to dry (March-May) and dry to rainy (September-November), shows a varied SIGMET distribution pattern. The analysis shows a concentration of activity in Papua and South Kalimantan, which is influenced by moisture transport, sea surface temperature (SST), and tropopause temperature. These factors support an unstable atmosphere and the formation of extreme weather phenomena. These findings provide important insights for further understanding of SIGMET distribution and its implications for aviation safety in Eastern Indonesia.", "2020"]

["Development of Irregular Interconnection Network Based on Graph Labeling", "One way for processors to communicate data is to use a shared memoryand shared variables. However this is unrealistic for large numbers of processors. A more realistic assumption is that each processor has its own private memory and data communication takes place using message passing through an interconnection network. The interconnection network plays a central role in determining the overall performance of a multicomputer system. An interconnection network may be modeled by a simple graph whose vertices represent components of the network and whose edges represent physical communication links, where directed edges represent one-way communication links and undirected edges represent two-way communication links, and the incidence function specifies a way that components of the network are interconnected by links. Such a graph is called the topological structure of the interconnection network, or network topology. Some interconnection network topologies are designed and some borrow from nature. For example hypercubes, complete binary trees, butterflies and torus networks are some of the designed architectures. Grids, hexagonal networks, honeycomb networks and diamond networks, for instance, bear resemblance to atomic or molecular lattice structures.They are called natural architectures. (Indra Rajasingh, Bharati Rajan, S. Teresa Arockiamary, Irregular total labeling of grid network, J.Comp. & Math. Sci. Vol. 2(6), 888-892w (2011) In this research, we will development interconnection network based on graph labeling, especially in total irregular interconnection network. The long term goal of this research is to enhance previous results that have been obtained by other researchers on the total edge irregularity strength ( tes ) and the total vertex irregularity strength ( tvs ) of any interconnection network system. As a special target of this research will be obtaine the total edge and the total vertex irregularity strength of the interconnection network system constructed by a diamond interconnection network. To achieve these objectives, the method used is to determine the total irregularity strength of diamond interconnection network with a partition separating to even and odd partitions. In general, the determination of the total irregularity strength will done in two stages, namely the first stage of the lower bound is determined by using the properties of the interconnection network. The second stage is to determine the upper bound by constructing a function on the interconnection network. Research will be conducted in Hasanuddin University Indonesia and in Technical University Kosice – Slovak Republic. In Hasanuddin University Indonesia, we will completely the first stage. Besides that, we will construction of special functions for the diamond interconnection network for simple cases. While the research will be carried out in Technical University Kosice to generalize results obtained to apply in general of complete diamond interconnection network. The study results will be written in the form paper and will be published to the Journal of Combinatorial Mathematics and Combinatorial Computing or Discrete Mathematics. Moreover, the results also will be presented at the International Conference on Educatioan, Mathematics, and Science 2016."]

["The edge irregular total labeling of the corona two any graphs", "A total edge irregular k-labeling of a graph G is defined as a mapping from the vertex set and the edge set of G to {1 , 2, 3,...,k} such that each edge of G has a distinct weight.The weight of an edge e=xy in E is the sum of the label of x, label of y and the label of e. The total edge irregularity strength of G, denoted by tes(G), is the smallest positive integer k such that G has a total edge irregular k-labeling. Determination of the total edge irregularity skength of a graph an easy matter because the tes(G) is greatly influenced by the structure and characteristics of the G. Until now only some graph class is already known its the total edge irregularity strength. Miskuf, J. and Jendrol, S (2007) gives the total edge irregularity strength of grids, Nurdin, Baskoro, E.T, Salman, A.N.M., Gaos, N.N (2006, 2008) gives the total edge irregularity strenght of union graph K_{2n}, the corona product of cycles with the complement of complete graphs, and the corona product of paths with some graphs. The goal this project we plan to determine the total edge irregularity strength of the corona product of any two graphs. In determining the total edge irregularity strenght of corona product of any graphs is used the results have been obtained by Baca et al. (2007) about the lower and above bound of the total edge irregularity strength of any graph. Before will be assessed on the properties of the corona product of graph . Technically, the determination of the total edge irregularity strength of the graph, the graph must be specified lower and upper bound. In determining the lower bound will be taken into account a certain number of edges. As for determining the upper bound, shall be constructed of an edge irregular total labeling on the graph. Of labeling that is constructed is shown that all the weights of its edges are different and the biggest number used is its the total edge irregularity strength."]

["Pelabelan Total Antiajaib Total dari Graf Hasil Operasi Amalgamasi Penuh Graf Regular dan Graf Lintasan", "Teori graf memainkan peran penting dalam berbagai bidang. ["Penerapan Pewarnaan Graf dalam Optimasi Komunikasi Data", "Perkembangan jaringan komunikasi dan internet global menuntut terjaminnya keamanan data dan penggunaan jaringan serta optimasi distribusi tugas dalam suatu jaringan. ["An investigation of factors affecting prediction of dayligh availability in high-rise residential buildings in a high density urban environment (2004-2008)", "", "This research investigates factors affecting the prediction of daylight availability in existing high-rise residential buildings located in high-density environments in order to develop a simplified daylight prediction method. To achieve this, several stages were completed. First, the daylight availability at an unobstructed area was evaluated, which involved collecting daylight data for a one-year period at the University of Hong Kong daylight station. Second, RADIANCE sky models were validated, based on scale model measurements and simulation results, to ensure their validity in modelling the local sky. Stage three was the investigation of factors affecting daylight prediction in high-rise residential buildings. Nineteen housing models representing eight plan types of existing residential buildings were selected. The Visible Sky Area (VSA), Vertical Sky Component (VSC) and Vertical Daylight Factor (VDF) were calculated for these buildings. VSC was used for defining the minimum VSA for Hong Kong. The final stage involved developing and validating a new daylight prediction method. Nine simple regression models and one multiple regression model were developed using statistical analyses based on the relation between the VDF and the VSA for different combinations of ground and building reflectances. All models were validated with RADIANCE using six hypothetical building layouts. To calculate the VSA, a calculation tool was constructed. The study found that the two most influential factors affecting the prediction of daylight availability on the window plane are the VSA and the surface reflectances. The VSA is affected by building forms and external obstructions. Most private housing estates have poor VSA’s, resulting in poor VDF performances. For each combination of ground and building reflectances, a very good correlation between VSA and VDF was found. The validation of the new method showed that some models accurately predicted the VDF, while others were less accurate. This study proposes three regression models together with a VSA calculation tool as a new daylight prediction method called the VSA Method for the Hong Kong Context."]

["FLEXURAL STRENGTH AND FAILURE PATTERN OF REINFORCED CONCREATE BEAMS WITH ANCHOR REINFORCEMENT, GROUTING, AND GFRP SHEET", "Corroded concrete can cause the spalling of area cover to problem and a reduction in reinforcement. ["STUDY OF THE LEVEL OF CORROSION OF STEEL SLATS CAUSED BY NATURAL EXPOSURE IN A CORROSIVE ENVIRONMENT IN MAKASSAR CITY AND PALU CITY", "Corrosion is a form of metal damage caused by electrochemical reactions in direct contact with the environment in the outside air, often referred to as atmospheric corrosion. ["Study of Reinforcement of Reinforced Concrete Beams Post Corrosion Using Grouting and GFRP Sheet", "There are many creative and unique ideas in construction design, especially in reinforced concrete construction where in reality a lot of building constructions show a decrease in structural strength, one of which is corrosion of the reinforcement. Grouting is the process of adding a mixture of water and Sika grout 215 because it has the characteristics of not shrinking, not corrosive, and can flow well so that it can easily fill small parts in concrete. Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) as a material that has high tensile strength, superior ductility, light weight so it is easy to mobilize, makes GFRP an option for structural repairs. This study aims to analyze the flexural behavior as well as crack patterns and failure modes of reinforced concrete beams reinforced with grouting and GFRP Sheet. The research method is testing the compressive strength of grouting mortar and flexural testing of reinforced concrete beams. Testing the compressive strength of grouting mortar using a cylindrical sample of 50 mm x 100 mm, tested at 28 days of age. Meanwhile, the bending test of beams used beam samples with dimensions of 150 mm x 200 mm x 3300 mm consisting of nine beams consisting of control beams (BK), beams with repair grouting (BGR), and beams with grouted mortar reinforcement and GFRP Sheet (BGRS). The results showed that the use of grouting mortar and GFRP sheet as repair and reinforcement materials can increase the maximum load of reinforced concrete beams. Meanwhile, the BGR beam has a more ductile behavior than all the test objects. From the connection failure mode, beams with mortar grouting reinforcement experience debonding failure while beams with grout reinforcement and GFRP sheet experience delamination failure and debonding failure at GFRP attachment."]

["Flexural Behavior Of Repaired Concrete Beam Using Grouting On Concrete Covers With Wiremesh Reinforcement", "As age and temperature increase, elements within structures can experience a decrease in quality due to several factors, one of which is environmental influence leading to corrosion. Previous studies have attempted to combine grouting materials with other reinforcement materials to produce repair material performance while also serving as reinforcement for beams, but this has been reported to fail. To address this shortfall, additional reinforcing steel with wire mesh is needed to enhance bonding performance and overall structural element durability. This study will examine the effect of wire mesh usage in repair concrete (grouting) with the aim of analyzing the flexural behavior of beams by observing crack patterns and failure modes in the beams. Flexural behavior is discussed based on load-deflection behavior, maximum load, steel strain-load, and concrete strain-load. The research stages involve flexural testing of beams using 150x200 mm beam samples with a length of 3300 mm, totaling 6 pieces consisting of a control beam, a normal grouting repair beam, and a grouting repair beam with wire mesh reinforcement, each with 2 pieces. The research results indicate that beams with grouting repair and the addition of wire mesh can increase the capacity of beams that have experienced spalling due to corrosion, but they are unable to surpass the capacity of the original beams. Regarding failure modes, beams reinforced with mortar grouting repair and wire mesh reinforcement experience flexural failure."]

["Studi Perilaku Lekatan Geser Abaca Fiber Reinforced Polymer Sheet pada Beton dengan Variasi Epoxy", "One of the methods to increase the structure\\'s capacity is repairing and strengthening. ["SHEAR BEHAVIOR OF REINFORCED CONCRETE BEAM WITH STREAP U-WRAP ABACA FIBER REINFORCED POLYMER SHEET", "Reinforced concrete structures are structures with the most use in the modern construction industry in the construction of infrastructure such as buildings, bridges and other structures. ["Karateristik Abaca Fiber Reinforced Polymer Sheet", "Global awareness of environmental issues is currently increasing, especially related to carbon emissions and biodiversity. ["Study of Capacity Calsium Board–Styrofoam Sandwich Panels on Wall Systems under Cyclic Lateral Force", "A new type of lightweight shear wall has been developed using composite panels, with styrofoam as the core layer and calcium board as the skin layer. ["Planning a Smart Waste Management System to Support the Smart City Concept: A Case Study of the ASN 4 Apartment Complex in Nusantara Capital City", "Waste is one of the complex issues faced by both developing and developed countries worldwide, including Indonesia. The concept of a smart city has emerged as a widely adopted solution in several countries. The world has been driven by the shift toward smart technologies to transform cities into smart cities, aiming to improve waste management, including in Nusantara Capital City, which is currently under development. This study aims to plan the development of a waste management system in Nusantara Capital City using the smart waste management system concept and conduct a comparative analysis between the existing conditions and the proposed development in terms of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The research was conducted using field observations and literature studies from various waste management documents as a standard for development. Additionally, a rapid carbon emission calculation was performed using the Emission Quantification Tool (EQT) developed by the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies (IGES). The results indicate that, under existing conditions, waste is not optimally sorted at the source, leading to waste accumulation and mixing. Waste sorting is only carried out at communal containers by the informal sector, resulting in a larger volume of waste disposed of at the landfill. In contrast, based on the development plan calculations, 42% of recyclable waste is sorted. This is attributed to the independent separation of recyclable waste at the source using waste bin shelters and the adoption of garbage chute technology to segregate organic and residual waste. Furthermore, 100% of waste processing is planned to utilize physical and thermal technologies at the Integrated Waste Treatment Facility (TPST), with 10% of the resulting Fly Ash and Bottom Ash (FABA) intended to be processed into building materials by third parties. Consequently, the carbon footprint of waste management activities under existing conditions results in GHG emissions of 1,173.49 kg CO₂-eq/ton , whereas the proposed development plan yields emissions of only 39.91 kg CO₂-eq/ton ."]

["Study of Floating Plastic Waste Potential in Kodingareng Lompo Island Using Multispectral Imagery from Sentinel-2A Satellite", "The issue of marine debris has become a global concern, with Indonesia significantly contributing to plastic pollution in the oceans. Plastic waste constitutes 60-80% of global marine debris, with Indonesia contributing up to 1.29 million tons annually, ranking fifth in terms of plastic waste entering the ocean. Ineffective waste management on land has led to the leakage of waste into the waters. The impact of plastic waste is extensive, threatening marine life, human health, and causing considerable economic losses. Remote sensing technologies, such as the Sentinel-2A satellite, offer solutions for more efficiently detecting and monitoring marine debris. This study utilizes Sentinel-2A imagery with various indices such as NDVI, NDWI, PI, and FDI to identify plastic debris around Pulau Kodingareng Lompo. Objective. This research aims to assess the capability of Sentinel-2 imagery in detecting and mapping potential plastic debris samples in Pulau Kodingareng Lompo. Method. The study involves adjusting the distribution maps generated by Sentinel-2 satellite based on the spread of plastic debris samples in the open sea, validated using spectral view and the SAV statistical method for the indices applied. Results. The Sentinel-2 data processing showed that four indices successfully detected plastic waste samples, with SAV values of 1.1, 0.1, 7.7, and 2.3, where PI had the highest value, making it the most representative in detecting floating plastic debris. Additionally, five plastic debris distribution hotspots were identified and validated using spectral view, which matched the characteristics of plastic waste. Conclusion. Sentinel-2 imagery successfully detected plastic debris samples in Kodingareng Lompo Island, with analysis using NDVI, NDWI, PI, and FDI indices showing SAV values of 1.1, 0.1, 7.7, and 2.3, with a reflectance range of 0.04 – 0.06 at the wavelength of band 8 (842 nm). The study also successfully identified five potential hotspots for plastic debris distribution around Pulau Kodingareng Lompo."]

["Study of Flat-Plate Solar Collector Integrated with Al-Foam and PCM Thermal Energy Storage (Doctoral Research Grant, 2024)", "Thermal energy storage (TES) as an energy storage technology is beneficial in limiting heat loss from solar collectors by absorbing excess heat from the absorber plates during peak hours of solar radiation. Phase change material (PCM) and metal foam are used to enhance the performance of solar water heating systems. This study examines how well flat-plate collectors work in a solar water heating system that is coupled to PCM energy storage components and aluminum-foam. This research investigated the impact of using aluminum-foam and PCM with paraffin-wax as thermal storage on a solar water heater (SWH) collector efficiency through an experimental analysis using three collector types. The first experiment is carried out without the use of thermal storage, while the remaining tests make use of thermal storage materials with a flow rate of 36 L/h, taking into consideration inlet and outlet temperatures. The research results demonstrate a comparison of collector efficiency between regular collector plates and modifications with thermal storage. Conventional collector plates have an efficiency of 84.19%, collector plates with aluminum-foam have an efficiency of 86.72%, and collector plates with aluminum-foam added by paraffin-wax have an efficiency of 91.88%. TES materials like aluminum-foam and paraffin-wax help to store energy and boost the heat transfer rate of the collector."]

["Photovoltaic-Based Water Heating System (Professor Research Grant, 2024)", "Solar energy is an energy source whose availability is guaranteed, renewable energy which has enormous potential in the future. In addition to lowering environmental pollutants, solar energy can be used directly or indirectly for heating. A photovoltaic-based water heating system (PVWHS) is designed to utilize solar energy into electrical energy using photovoltaic cells, which are then connected to a DC heating element to heat the water in the tank. Testing this tool uses experimental methods to identify the optimal temperature of water, the energy needed to heat the water and thermal efficiency of the PVWHS. The test was carried-out using polycrystal photovoltaic cells and by varying the volume of the water tank, namely 10 liters, 15 liters and 25 liters. The results of this research show that a 10 liters water tank volume can increase the average water temperature by 10.7˚C. And a water tank volume of 15 liters can increase the average water temperature by 8.1˚C, and a water tank volume of 25 liters can increase the average water temperature by 5.6˚C. The efficiency of polycrystal photovoltaic cells was found to be an average efficiency of 7.34%. Meanwhile, the maximum heater efficiency was found to be 73.6% for all variations of water tanks. As for the maximum total efficiency value, the overall system efficiency is 5.35% for all water tank variations."]

["Investigation of Solar Water Heating System using Flat-plate Absorber Integrated with Composite Thermal Storage (PDUPT Research Grant, 2022)", "The solar water heating (SWH) technology is a cost-effective method of harnessing solar energy and widely used in various countries worldwide. Adding thermal storage to the flat-plate collector increases the performance of the SWH system. It contributes to reduce energy loss to the top and increases energy transfer to the water. A novel composite material as thermal storage integrated with a flat-plate collector is constructed to make it effective in absorbing and storing heat energy. This work aims to investigate the performance of SWH system by integrating Al + Al2O3 composite to the flat-plate collector at the bottom as thermal storage. The performances of two models of absorber plates including a standard flat-plate collector and with Al + Al2O3 composite as thermal storage are investigated experimentally. The Al + Al2O3 composites were also tested and characterized to obtain their thermal properties. The results show that adding Al + Al2O3 composite as the thermal storage to the absorber plate contributes to increase absorption of solar irradiation, heat storage, and thermal efficiency of the collector. Then, the collector model with Al + Al2O3 composite as the thermal storage provides higher thermal efficiency than that of the standard model. For example, the thermal efficiency of the collector model with composite thermal storage of alumina 35% and aluminum 65% at angle variation increase of 5.1 % (0◦), 7.5 % (10◦), and 2.5 % (30◦). Thermal properties of Al + Al2O3 composites as the thermal storage are also presented. It concludes that the greater percentage of alumina content, the lower value of the thermal properties of the composite obtained."]

["Effect of Thermal Storage on the Performance of the Flat-Plate Solar Collector (PDUPT Research Grant, 2023)", "The use of solar energy for hot water supply through solar water heating (SWH) systems is gaining popularity due to its eco-friendly technology. Integrating heat storage in SWH systems under conditions of low solar radiation is one of the cutting-edge technical approaches in this field. The direct utilization of stored thermal energy has recently drawn attention to compact and integrated solar thermal storage-collector systems. The goal of this project is to look into how the thickness of storage changes the performance of flat-plate solar collectors. It is also looked into how thermal storage affects the system\\'s thermal performance when the weather is unclear. Experiments and computer simulations are used to look into how well combined flat-plate solar collectors work with different thicknesses of thermal storage. To learn more about the features of thermal storage, numerical models were run to see how the thickness of the storage affected performance."]

["Study of Modified Absorber Plate Integrated with Aluminium Foam of Solar Water Heating System (Laboratory-Based Education (LBE) Research Fund 2021)", "The Solar Water Heating System (SWHS) is a water heater equipment that utilizes solar energy for domestic scale needs. The potential generated by this system can reduce the energy demand of the building sector, reduce peak demand for electricity, and reduction in pollution. This study aims to analyze the performance of SWHS experimentally by modifying the addition of aluminium foam material at the bottom of the absorber plate and the top of the absorber plate. The absorber plate models are Standard Flat-Plate (SFP), SFP with Bottom Aluminium Foam (SFP-BAF), and SFP with Top Aluminium Foam (SFP-TAF). The experimental study was carried out for the three models under similar conditions using a Solar Thermal Energy Unit. The effect of flowrate variations and slope angles were also investigated. The study results show that the SFP-BAF model with the angle of 30o achieved the highest efficiency of 88.4%, 86.9%, and 83.9% at a flow rate of 8 L/h, 10 L/h, and 12 L/h, respectively. The benefits of adding aluminium foam to the absorber plate is to increase the absorption of radiant heat energy transmitted from the absorber plate, the storage time of thermal energy, and the thermal efficiency of the collector."]

["Development of IoT-Based Ecoprint Automation System with Real-Time Monitoring and Remote Control", "Eco-Tech Revolution: Weaving the Future of Sustainable Textiles with AI and IoT The world of fashion and textiles is standing at a crossroads. ["Offline HTML5 automation learning and service workers to overcome unreliable network connectivity in web-based systems for Small and Medium Industries (SMEs) in rural areas", "Empowering the Heart of Rural Commerce: Training Without Borders In the modern era, we often take for granted the invisible threads that connect us to the world: the internet. For many of us, a flickering Wi-Fi signal is a minor inconvenience. However, for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) located in rural or remote areas, a \"poor connection\" is more than just a nuisance—it is a digital wall that halts progress, stunts growth, and limits the potential of hardworking local communities. This research addresses a critical gap in digital equity. While the world moves toward sophisticated cloud-based learning management systems, rural SMEs are often left behind because their infrastructure cannot support the heavy data demands of these platforms. When an employee in a remote village tries to access a training module to improve their skills, a buffering screen isn't just a technical glitch; it is a lost opportunity for economic advancement. Our solution reimagines how web applications behave in challenging environments. By leveraging the power of HTML5 and Service Workers , we have developed a resilient web application that effectively \"defies\" the unstable network. Think of a Service Worker as a smart, tireless digital assistant living inside your browser. This assistant works behind the scenes to intercept network requests. When the internet is active, it quietly downloads and stores essential training materials. The moment the connection drops, the Service Worker takes over, serving the content from a local cache seamlessly. For the user, the experience remains uninterrupted. They can continue their automated learning journey, take assessments, and interact with the interface as if they were in the middle of a high-tech city. This is not just a website; it is an intelligent, self-sustaining ecosystem designed for the reality of rural life. This research is deeply rooted in the United Nations’ vision for a better world. Specifically, this project is a direct contribution to Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4): Quality Education . While SDG 4 is often associated with traditional schooling, its broader mission is to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. By removing the \"internet barrier,\" we are democratizing access to professional development. We believe that a weaver in a remote forest or a farmer managing a small cooperative deserves the same quality of training as a corporate executive in a skyscraper. By facilitating continuous, automated learning, we empower SME employees to upgrade their skills, improve their productivity, and eventually increase their standard of living. This technological intervention ensures that \"Quality Education\" is not a privilege reserved for those with fiber-optic cables, but a right accessible to anyone with a basic smartphone and the will to learn. By bridging the digital divide, we are doing more than just fixing a \"web page.\" We are building the digital resilience of rural communities. When SMEs thrive through better-trained staff, entire local economies stabilize. This project proves that high-level computer science—specifically the implementation of service workers and offline-first architectures—has a very human face. It is about ensuring that in our race toward a high-tech future, the heart of our rural communities is never left in the dark. Through this innovation, the path to knowledge remains open, stable, and smooth, regardless of the strength of the signal. ["Paleoceanographic Reconstruction Based on Nannofossils of Tonasa Formation South Sulawesi, Ristek-Dikti", "The Tonasa Limestone Formation in this area consists of interbedded marl and limestone, which developed extensively in a marine environment from the Late Eocene to Oligocene. ["Inventory and Distribution of Micro Fossils and Paleogeographic Implications of Tonasa Formation, Jeneponto Regency, South Sulawesi Province, Hasanuddin University Internal Grant", "The biostratigraphy of the Tonasa Formation in Jeneponto Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, remains poorly understood, with significant gaps in age records, particularly throughout much of the Oligocene to Early Miocene. In this region, the formation consists of interbedded marl and limestone. Our study focuses on the biostratigraphy of Section A in the Karama area, using calcareous nannofossils as biostratigraphic markers. Samples were collected using measured stratigraphy methods and analyzed through smear slide preparation. The species assemblages were identified using a semi-quantitative approach. The data analysis revealed three key nannofossil datum levels (boundaries): The First Occurrence (FO) of Sphenolithus pseudoradians (NP19/NP20) The First Occurrence (FO) of Sphenolithus distentus (CP16/CP17) The Last Occurrence (LO) of Sphenolithus predistentus (NP23/NP24) The zonal boundary, determined based on calcareous nannoplankton, indicates that the Tonasa Formation in this section spans from the Late Eocene to the Middle Oligocene. Notably, Sphenolithus serves as the primary marker species throughout this period. Furthermore, the presence of Sphenolithus , Discoaster, and Zygrhablithus bijugatus suggests that the basin experienced warm water conditions during deposition."]

["Konsep dan Pradisain Coastal Settlement Koridor Ekologi dan Sosial: Solusi Multi-Fungsi untuk Resilience Permukiman Pesisir (tahap 2)", "SUMMARY MAKASSAR, Indonesia, September 17, 2026/CSR/ – Tidal flooding, or coastal flooding caused by high tides, is becoming an increasingly frequent threat in coastal areas, particularly in low-lying regions, with wide-ranging impacts. This phenomenon, driven by extreme tidal conditions, sea-level rise, and land subsidence, disrupts socio-economic activities, damages infrastructure, and threatens the sustainability of coastal settlements. Climate change, including rising ocean temperatures and polar ice loss, further exacerbates these risks, making coastal areas, including Indonesia, highly vulnerable. In addition, coastal erosion and ecosystem degradation further increase vulnerability. Therefore, the development of a multifunctional ecological and social corridor may provide an innovative approach to addressing these challenges. This concept integrates environmental protection with the provision of social spaces, such as parks, pedestrian pathways, and recreational facilities, to reduce disaster risks while improving community quality of life. The approach supports the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), by strengthening the resilience of coastal areas to climate change and natural hazards. The challenges faced by coastal areas differ between urban areas such as Makassar and rural areas such as Minasamaupata. Makassar, which is experiencing rapid urbanization and increasing population density, is vulnerable to tidal flooding and coastal erosion, while Minasamaupata, where communities depend heavily on fisheries, faces threats to socio-economic resilience due to ecosystem degradation. Developing multifunctional ecological and social corridors in both areas could strengthen climate resilience through mangrove rehabilitation and the provision of social infrastructure adapted to local needs. Collaboration among government institutions, local communities, and the private sector is essential for creating more resilient and sustainable coastal settlements. Long-Term Objectives In the long term, the development of a coastal corridor based on multifunctional vegetation and recreational embankments is expected to provide multiple benefits for environmental resilience and community well-being. Through the planting and restoration of appropriate coastal vegetation, the area will become more resilient to sea-level rise and coastal erosion, thereby strengthening the climate resilience of coastal environments. The corridor will also function as an embankment that not only protects inland areas from tidal flooding but also provides public spaces for activities such as jogging, cycling, and recreation. The social corridor within the area may support local economic development based on ecotourism and sustainable fisheries, creating new livelihood opportunities for local communities. The availability of green public spaces and social infrastructure is also expected to improve residents' quality of life, reduce health risks associated with tidal flooding, and create a safer and more comfortable living environment. The success of this strategy will depend strongly on multistakeholder collaboration involving government institutions, local communities, academics, and the private sector to establish an inclusive and sustainable model of coastal governance. In addition to providing social and economic benefits, the corridor will contribute to maintaining coastal ecosystem balance, protecting biodiversity, and strengthening the adaptive capacity of ecosystems to climate change. Through an integrated approach, this strategy is expected to provide a sustainable long-term solution to environmental and social challenges in coastal areas. Specific Targets The following specific targets are proposed through the development of a multifunctional vegetation-based coastal corridor and recreational embankment in North Galesong: 1. Climate and Environmental Resilience Reduction of coastal erosion by X% within Y years through the planting of coastal vegetation that is resilient to marine waves. Reduction of tidal flooding impacts by increasing the capacity of multifunctional embankments to withstand high-tide water levels. Expansion of coastal vegetation coverage by X hectares to strengthen shoreline protection and enhance biodiversity. 2. Sustainable Economic Empowerment Increase in coastal community income by X% through ecotourism and sustainable fisheries supported by the social corridor. Creation of X new employment opportunities in ecotourism, fisheries, and related supporting services. Development of local micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) based on coastal products and nature-based tourism to improve community livelihoods. Methods The research methods will employ several approaches to investigate biomimicry-based solutions for managing tidal flooding in North Galesong: 1. Geographic Information System (GIS) GIS will be used to map geographical conditions, topography, and shoreline changes to understand the spatial patterns and impacts of coastal erosion and tidal flooding. 2. Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) AHP will be used to determine the priority of mitigation strategies based on environmental, economic, and social factors. 3. Surveys and Interviews Surveys and interviews will be conducted to collect socio-economic data, assess community perceptions, and identify local needs and potentials for implementing coastal adaptation strategies. These methods will be applied in an integrated manner to develop effective and sustainable biomimicry-based solutions for addressing tidal flooding and strengthening coastal resilience. Alignment with the UNHAS Strategic Plan The development of a multifunctional vegetation-based coastal corridor and recreational embankment in North Galesong is aligned with the Strategic Plan (Renstra) of Hasanuddin University (UNHAS) 2020–2024 in several respects: 1. Development of Science and Technology Based on the Indonesian Maritime Continent (BMI) UNHAS is committed to becoming a center of excellence for the development of science and technology focusing on the Indonesian Maritime Continent (Benua Maritim Indonesia/BMI). This project supports this commitment by investigating biomimicry-based solutions for tidal-flood mitigation, which are highly relevant to environmental challenges in maritime regions. 2. Multistakeholder Collaboration The UNHAS Strategic Plan emphasizes collaboration among government institutions, academia, communities, and the private sector. The proposed coastal corridor initiative involves multiple stakeholders and seeks to establish an inclusive and sustainable model of coastal governance. 3. Community Empowerment and Community Engagement UNHAS places emphasis on community engagement through the downstream application of research and the delivery of research-based benefits to society. This project has the potential to improve the well-being of coastal communities through ecotourism and sustainable fisheries, in line with the university's commitment to community empowerment. Accordingly, the project not only supports UNHAS's vision of becoming a center of excellence in science and technology development based on the Indonesian Maritime Continent but also strengthens the university's role in community engagement and multistakeholder collaboration. By recognizing the importance of integrating environmental management with socio-economic planning, this research aims to explore multifunctional solutions for strengthening the resilience of coastal settlements to climate change while improving the quality of life of coastal communities. ["Model Konseptual Jaringan Sanitasi Black Water Berbasis Smart Bio-Reactor dengan Modular Wetland System di Ruang Komunal sebagai Solusi Berkelanjutan untuk Resiliensi Permukiman Pesisir", "Coastal water settlements, particularly in developing countries, face serious sanitation challenges due to limited domestic wastewater treatment infrastructure. This situation is exacerbated by the direct discharge of wastewater into water bodies, which leads to environmental degradation, pollution of seawater and shallow groundwater, and an increased risk of water-borne diseases such as diarrhea, skin infections, and gastrointestinal diseases. In the long term, this practice not only threatens public health but also damages coastal ecosystems and local fisheries productivity. Conventional sanitation systems, such as large-scale wastewater treatment plants and centralized piped systems, are generally difficult to implement in coastal settlements due to several factors. First, limited land and dense housing hinder large-scale infrastructure development. Second, dynamic hydrological conditions, such as tides, tidal flooding, and seawater intrusion, make conventional sanitation systems prone to failure. Third, limited access to environmentally friendly and affordable wastewater treatment technologies is a major obstacle to comprehensively improving blackwater sanitation. Therefore, a blackwater sanitation approach is needed that is not only adaptive to the challenges of the physical and spatial environment but also appropriate to the socio-economic conditions of coastal communities. The Smart Bio-Reactor approach offers an efficient and compact biotechnology-based alternative for domestic wastewater treatment. This technology enables faster biological decomposition and can be scaled to small settlements. Meanwhile, the Modular Wetland System (MWS) provides a natural filtration system utilizing aquatic vegetation and substrate media to remove pollutants sustainably and based on natural ecosystems. The integration of these two approaches into a conceptual model for a sanitation network provides the opportunity to create a modular, flexible, and resilient system that adapts to coastal environmental changes. This model not only aims to improve the efficiency of domestic wastewater treatment but also strengthens the ecological and social resilience of communities living near waterways. Its placement in communal spaces allows for a decentralized system. Its decentralized nature also supports community participation, particularly by families, in blackwater sanitation management and allows for scalability to meet local needs. This research focuses on the conceptual stage, aiming to design and develop a hybrid sanitation network based on the Smart Bio-Reactor and the Modular Wetland System as an adaptive and sustainable sanitation solution in tropical coastal areas. The results of this conceptual phase are expected to form the basis for developing a prototype system and replication in other coastal settlements with similar characteristics. This long-term goal aligns with the SDGs, specifically: • Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), • Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and • Goal 13 (Climate Action). Overall, the long-term goal of developing a sanitation system based on the Smart Bio-Reactor and Modular Wetland System in communal spaces aligns with the global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) agenda. First, this initiative supports Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) by providing an innovative, efficient, and affordable domestic wastewater treatment solution for coastal settlements that currently experience limited access to adequate sanitation infrastructure. Second, the implementation of this system strengthens Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) by contributing to the creation of inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable settlements through an ecologically based architectural and spatial planning approach and community participation. Third, the integration of natural systems in graywater treatment also supports Goal 13 (Climate Action) by increasing communities' adaptive capacity to the impacts of climate change, such as tidal flooding and seawater intrusion, while simultaneously reducing the ecological footprint through low-emission, locally resource-based technologies. Thus, this concept not only offers a technical solution but also builds the foundation for a healthy, resilient, and environmentally just residential ecosystem."]

["RKI (Riset Kolaborasi Indonesia) : Coastal Settlement Resilience: Stilt Housing Adaptation to Urbanization Pressure and Space Constraints in Coastal Communities.", "Rapid urbanization in Indonesia’s coastal areas has led to increasing population density and limited land availability. According to data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS), the urbanization rate reached 57% in 2021 and is projected to rise to 66% by 2045, with approximately 40% of Indonesia’s population living in coastal regions. In response to this pressure, communities have adapted by innovating two-story stilt housing that optimizes vertical space while supporting socio-economic sustainability. Social resilience is demonstrated through changing patterns of interaction and the use of space beneath the houses as communal areas, while economic resilience is reflected in livelihood diversification, such as utilizing the underfloor space for small-scale businesses. From an infrastructural perspective, multi-level housing and the use of environmentally friendly materials contribute to improved environmental resilience. Ecologically, biomimicry is applied in housing design to address challenges such as coastal abrasion and tidal flooding. Case studies from the coastal settlements of Cambayya in Makassar, Kalibaru in Jakarta, and Lumpur in Gresik illustrate how communities adapt by building stilt houses over water using recycled materials. However, these areas still face major challenges such as abrasion, poor sanitation, and disaster risk. Solutions such as more robust two-story stilt housing and improvements in sanitation infrastructure and clean water access are needed to enhance community well-being. This study aims to analyze the spatial adaptation patterns of housing and settlements in Cambayya, Kalibaru, and Gresik in response to urbanization; evaluate the effectiveness of two-story stilt houses; and develop strategies for sustainable coastal settlement development. Employing a constructivist paradigm and a mixed-methods research approach, this study combines descriptive and exploratory methods to understand adaptation strategies and the effectiveness of infrastructure in enhancing the social, economic, and ecological resilience of coastal communities."]
