["Modeling and simulation of low-speed wind power for vertical axis wind turbine generator with computer fluid dynamic", "The nation is experiencing an energy crisis, with more energy needs but limited sources. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), this crisis can be overcome by switching to new renewable energy sources. Wind energy is one of Indonesia\\'s latest renewable sources and has excellent potential. The challenge in Indonesia in utilizing wind energy is the relatively low wind speed. This research aims to design and simulate a vertical-axis wind turbine design for low wind speeds by knowing the turbine\\'s performance in the form of power coefficient values and output power. This research was conducted by designing a Darrieus type vertical axis turbine using airfoil variations and variations in the number of blades. For the placement of vertical wind turbines as the windfarm configuration, there is an increase in output power of 11.87% after changing the position from inline to staggered."]

["Plan design of floating PV systems in Mawang Lake with PVSyst Software Applications", "Indonesia\\'s increasing demand for renewable energy faces the challenge of limited land availability for ground-mounted solar power plants. The Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) technology offers an efficient solution by utilizing water surfaces for solar panel installation, thereby reducing the need for land. This study aims to analyze the development potential of FSPV in Lake Mawang, Gowa Regency, as a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative energy source. The research utilizes solar irradiation data from Meteonorm 8.1 and simulations using PVsyst software to calculate system capacity, energy production, and system efficiency and losses. The findings indicate that FSPV has significant potential for implementation in Indonesia, particularly in areas with limited land, and can support clean energy sustainability and carbon emission reduction efforts. This study provides a strong technical foundation for further developing FSPV systems in Indonesia."]

["Determination of wind speed for wind power generation with Hellmann coefficient and Roughness Length", "Using wind power plants as a renewable energy source requires wind at a certain speed to drive wind turbines and generate electrical energy. The surface and topography factors greatly influence the optimal wind turbine speed in the area. This study aims to provide an overview of the influence of surface type and topography in an area related to wind speed variations, which can be used as a reference in the design and planning of new wind power stations. The results show that surface and topographic factors significantly affect wind speed variation in a location. In the Jeneponto Offshore location, calm sea levels allow for high wind speeds at low altitudes. At the same time, areas such as Bone and Takalar with rice paddy surfaces show higher resistivity to wind, resulting in slower surface wind speeds. The use of Power Law and Logarithmic Law as an initial solution to predict wind speeds at higher altitudes, along with the integration of new wind power stations and energy storage systems, can increase the utilization of renewable energy and meet the electricity needs in the South Sulawesi region."]

["Research Project: Smart Ergonomic Workstations for Enhanced Well-Being", "The HES Research Group is developing Smart Ergonomic Workstations designed to improve posture, reduce fatigue, and enhance productivity in various work environments. This project integrates AI-driven posture correction, adaptive furniture, and real-time environmental adjustments to create a user-centered workspace that promotes health and efficiency. By utilizing wearable sensors and machine learning algorithms , the system provides personalized ergonomic recommendations based on user behavior and movement patterns. Features include automated desk and chair height adjustments, optimal lighting control, and posture monitoring to prevent musculoskeletal disorders. The research involves collaboration with industry partners, healthcare professionals, and technology developers to refine and implement these smart solutions in offices, industrial settings, and home workspaces. The project aims to set new standards for ergonomic workplace design , ensuring comfort, safety, and productivity for workers of all ages and abilities. Future applications include healthcare, education, and remote work environments."]

["Maneuvering performance of Indonesian ro-ro ferries (2014 – 2016)", "This research aims to investigate the maneuvering performance of a ship with small draught and large breadth during operation. The effect of wind and waves was analyzed to obtain the controllability and operational limitation of an Indonesian ro-ro ferry. An autopilot control system using PID control has been designed and verified with free running model experiment. The estimation fuel consumption corresponding to the operational condition has been conducted in a certain operational route of an Indonesian ro-ro ferry. This work is necessary to validate with the real operational condition by directly measure the fuel consumption of the ship. The results can be used to estimate the exhaust emission in relation to the energy efficiency design index (EEDI) or energy efficiency operation index (EEOI) as well as the contribution of the Indonesian ro-ro ferries on air pollution."]

["Intact stability criteria for Unconventional Ships in Indonesia (2019 – 2021)", "The stability criteria used to assess merchant ships stability is the International Stability Criteria of International Maritime Organization (IMO). That criteria are applied to convention ship with internationally operated. A different criteria may be used to unconventional ship and locally operated. Each country may developed their own local stability criteria even thought the criteria of IMO still may be used. The objective of this research are to develop intact stability criteria applied to ships operating in Indonesia, namely the Indonesian ro-ro ferries and the Indonesian traditional wooden boats. The breadth-to-draught ratio of an Indonesian ro-ro ferry may be larger than 4.5. The Indonesian traditional wooden boats were built with not watertight main deck construction. Therefore the down flooding angle can be small than 30 degrees or the angle with maximum righting arm."]

["Overthrowing phenomena of a vehicles in Indonesian ro-ro ferries (2022 – 2024)", "The accidents frequently occur on Indonesian ro-ro ferries are shifting or overthrowing of vehicles loaded in the main deck. The accidents could be induced by the large lateral acceleration during the ship operation in rough weather. The International Maritime Organization has been included the lateral acceleration as one of vulnerability mode in the Second Generation Intact Stability Criteria (SGISC) known as the excessive acceleration criteria. Most of Indonesian ro-ro ferries fulfill the requirements of a ship to be tested against the excessive acceleration criteria, namely the metacentric height (GM) and the location of passenger and crew accommodation. The research aims to investigate the possibility of a truck shifting or overthrowing. The results can be used to determined the operational limitation of an Indonesian ro-ro ferry correspond to the lateral acceleration induce car shifting or overthrowing. The results by also be used to design lashing construction to avoid that accident."]

["Floating structures for energy conversion at sea (2023 – 2024)", "The present research project conducted corresponds to ocean energy conversion is design of floating structure for wave energy conversion. The efficiency depends on the wave and floating body characteristics. Numerical analysis was performed to estimate the heave motion of some different shape and geometry characteristics of floating structure. The body was designed to be multi function as wave energy conversion and as mooring buoy or navigation buoy in port area or ship route to enter the port. The main purpose is to find out the most efficient floating body to convert wave energy for a certain wave characteristics, namely the wave heigh and wave length. The results may also be used to determine the buoy dimension correspond to the wave characteristics of a certain area/location. The research corresponds to the pitch motion of a SPAR to be used as a floating structure for ocean wind turbine. Vertical damping plate with various number and configuration has been investigate its impact on the damping moment of pitch motion by model experiment. Numerical simulation of pitch motion with variation of damping plate configuration has also been performed to analysis the effect on the pitch motion. The results show that the damping plate in a certain condition can significantly reduce the pitch motion of the SPAR."]

["Transforming Makassar Port: A Roadmap Toward a Sustainable Green Port", "2025", "This study explores the potential for implementing green port strategies at Makassar Port to balance economic growth with environmental protection. Using SWOT analysis , the study found Makassar Port in Quadrant I , indicating strong potential to pursue aggressive sustainability strategies. Key priorities include energy efficiency, cleaner operations, environmental management, and stakeholder collaboration , supporting SDG 14: Life Below Water and a more sustainable maritime future."]

["The Air We Cannot See: What Makassar’s Busy Roads Reveal About Public Health", "2025", "This study examines air quality and public health perceptions on six arterial roads in Makassar , focusing on NH₃, NO₂, and PM₁₀. Although pollutant concentrations remained below air-quality standards, some respondents reported coughing and dizziness , with 36% reporting frequent coughing near Perintis Kemerdekaan and A.P. Pettarani. The findings highlight the importance of combining air-quality measurements with public perception to support cleaner transportation and healthier cities in line with SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being ."]

["Every Journey Has a Hidden Cost: The Emissions Behind Urban Transportation", "2015", "This article explores transportation emissions, particularly CO₂, and how vehicle type, traffic conditions, fuel consumption, and driving patterns influence emission levels. Based on the book Emisi Transportasi: Kuantitas Emisi Berdasarkan MARNI Model by Sumarni Hamid Aly , it highlights the MARNI Model as a tool for estimating emissions from heterogeneous traffic. The discussion emphasizes the importance of emission assessment in supporting SDG 3 by promoting healthier communities through cleaner and more sustainable transportation."]

["Beneath the Traffic Jam: The Carbon Cost of Makassar’s Busiest Road", "2022", "This study examines CO₂ emissions from motorized vehicles on the 4.2-km Urip Sumoharjo Road in Makassar , divided into six segments. Results show the highest emissions occurred during the afternoon rush hour (5:00–6:00 p.m.) , particularly in Segments 6, 5, and 1. Motorcycles and sedans were the largest contributors, with a strong correlation between vehicle volume and CO₂ emissions ( r = 0.916 ). The findings highlight the importance of efficient transportation and traffic management to support SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being ."]

["The Hidden Cost of Traffic: How Vehicle Emissions Threaten Public Health in Makassar", "2023", "Every day, thousands of people travel across Makassar City, contributing to air pollution from vehicle emissions. A study on ten collector roads identified four major pollutants: NOx, SO₂, PM₁₀, and CO . Using the Tier 2 emission calculation method , the study found that Letjen Hertasning Road had the highest emission load, with CO exceeding 104,000 tons/year . High traffic volume and congestion were major factors increasing emissions, particularly from light vehicles and minibuses."]

["Beyond the Traffic Jam: Turning Scientific Data into Smarter Cities", "2025", "This study examines the relationship between vehicle volume and PM₁₀ concentrations across 16 road sections in Makassar City. Using HVAS measurements and regression analysis, the study found that all observation points exceeded Indonesia’s PM₁₀ ambient air quality standard. The findings highlight the influence of other factors, such as vehicle speed, road characteristics, and weather conditions, and emphasize the importance of collaboration among researchers, government, and stakeholders in achieving sustainable urban development under SDG 17."]

["When Every Street Tells A Story: Using Science And Collaboration To Reduce Urban Vehicle Emissions", "2026", "This study evaluates vehicle-related air pollution along Pengayoman Street, Makassar , focusing on diesel-powered light-duty vehicles. Using traffic volume, speed, travel distance, and travel time data from 14 road segments, the IPCC Tier 2 and MARNI models were applied and compared using RMSE. The results show that traffic congestion and afternoon peak-hour conditions significantly increase emissions , with CO₂ and NOₓ as the dominant pollutants. The study highlights how scientific modeling, field observations, and cross-sector collaboration can support evidence-based transportation planning and contribute to SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals ."]

["Seeing the Invisible: How Satellites Are Helping Makassar Fight Air Pollution", "2026", "This study highlights the use of Landsat 8 satellite imagery, ground-based PM₁₀ measurements, and multiple linear regression to estimate and map PM₁₀ concentrations across Makassar City. Using data from 30 monitoring locations, the study demonstrates that satellite-based modeling can provide reliable spatial information on air pollution, particularly through the integration of Bands 1–4. The research also emphasizes the importance of collaboration among researchers, governments, technology providers, and communities , supporting evidence-based environmental management and contributing to SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals ."]

["Eyes in the Sky, Guardians on the Ground: How Satellite Technology Is Revolutionizing Air Quality Monitoring Around Indonesia's Cement Industry", "2026", "This study combines Landsat 8 satellite imagery and field measurements to assess PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and CO concentrations at 41 locations in a cement industrial area of Pangkep, South Sulawesi. Satellite data successfully identified pollution hotspots around industrial facilities , although some concentrations were overestimated compared with field measurements. The findings highlight the potential of remote sensing as a cost-effective early-warning and air quality monitoring tool , supporting SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) ."]

["Invisible Danger on Our Roads: How Science is Mapping Carbon Monoxide to Protect Urban Health", "2025", "Carbon monoxide (CO) pollution in Makassar City was assessed using field measurements and AERMOD dispersion modeling across 30 locations and five road categories. The study found that major roads with high traffic generally produced the highest CO emissions, while road characteristics such as width, length, and surrounding structures also influenced pollutant concentrations. The strong agreement between modeled and measured CO levels demonstrates the potential of AERMOD to map pollution hotspots and support urban planning, traffic management, and public health protection ."]

["Watching the Air from Space: How Satellite Technology Can Help Build Healthier Cities", "2025", "Satellite-based air quality monitoring in Makassar Metropolitan City combines Landsat 8 and MODIS imagery with Land Surface Temperature (LST) to estimate seasonal NO₂ concentrations . The study found higher NO₂ levels during the dry season and a strong relationship between higher LST and increased pollution. Rappocini, Mariso, Panakkukang, and Biringkanaya showed the highest concentrations, while greener and coastal areas generally had lower levels. The findings highlight the potential of remote sensing to complement ground monitoring, identify pollution hotspots, and support healthier and more sustainable urban management ."]

["Analysis of PM10 Distribution Patterns from Motor Vehicle Emissions at 30 Points in Makassar City", "2025", "This study focuses on air pollution in Makassar City, which is largely caused by motor vehicle emissions. The growth in the number of motor vehicles, which reached more than 2 million units in 2024, has led to high levels of particulate matter (PM₁₀) in the ambient air, which has a direct impact on public health. The research was conducted by measuring PM₁₀ concentrations at 30 locations in Makassar City using a High Volume Air Sampler (HVAS) for 15 days, with four time intervals (morning, afternoon, evening, and night). In addition, vehicle volume was also calculated based on type (motorcycles, light vehicles, and heavy vehicles). Secondary data in the form of meteorological parameters were obtained from Climate Copernicus. The analysis was continued with emission load calculations using the Tier-2 method based on vehicle emission factors, as well as pollutant dispersion modeling using AERMOD software. PM10 emission dispersion modeling was performed using AERMOD software, which produced a map of PM10 concentration distribution in the analyzed area. PM10 dispersion was visualized using color gradations on isopleths or contour maps showing variations in concentration levels, where different colors represent different gas concentration levels. Light blue to green colors represent low concentrations or low pollution levels, yellow represents moderate concentrations, orange represents fairly high concentrations, red represents high concentrations, and dark red to purple represents very high concentrations in the area. This distribution pattern produces an output in the form of an isopleth map, which consists of contour lines connecting points with the same concentration. This isopleth map is applied in the Makassar City area to illustrate the distribution of PM10 over 24 hours at 30 receptor points, with concentration differences displayed in various shapes and colors according to the amount of emissions in the area. The results of the study show that: The PM₁₀ concentration from direct measurements was in the range of 108–258 µg/m³, while the modeling results showed a range of 103–418 µg/m³. The PM₁₀ emission load from mobile sources on the road ranged from 0.01–1.54 g/s, with the largest contribution coming from heavy vehicles. The distribution pattern of PM₁₀ follows the prevailing wind direction to the northwest, so that areas along this route have the potential for higher pollution. Based on Government Regulation No. 22 of 2021, the ambient air quality in Makassar has exceeded the PM₁₀ quality standard (75 µg/m³ for 24 hours), posing a health hazard. This study emphasizes the importance of controlling motor vehicle emissions and utilizing air quality modeling as an alternative monitoring method. The results can be used as consideration for local governments in formulating urban transportation management and air quality protection policies."]

["Satellite Imagery-Based PM₁₀ Air Parameter Analysis in Makassar City", "2025", "The study entitled “Analysis of PM₁₀ Air Parameters Based on Satellite Images in Makassar City” was conducted to address serious challenges related to urban air pollution. Makassar City, as the center of economic and governmental activities in Eastern Indonesia, has experienced a significant increase in the number of motor vehicles—more than 2 million units in 2024. This condition has a direct impact on air quality, particularly the increased concentration of PM₁₀ particulates, which can cause respiratory health problems and reduce the quality of the living environment. Conventional air quality monitoring in Makassar City is still limited because there are very few Air Quality Monitoring Stations (SPKU) and they are unable to describe the distribution of pollutants evenly. Therefore, this study utilizes remote sensing technology using Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery processed with Google Earth Engine (GEE). PM₁₀ concentration estimates were made by applying two popular algorithms, namely Othman (2010) and Mozafari (2019). The research method consisted of two main stages: Field data collection through PM₁₀ measurements at 30 sampling points throughout the subdistricts of Makassar City using a High Volume Air Sampler (HVAS) in accordance with SNI 7119.15:2016. Satellite image processing to extract PM₁₀ concentrations based on the Landsat 8 spectral band, followed by validation using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) test against field measurement results. The results of the study show that: The highest PM₁₀ concentrations in the field were found at Pasar Baru Daya (262.9 µg/m³), Makassar Town Square Mall (258.0 µg/m³), and Galangan Kapal (243.6 µg/m³). The satellite estimation results showed differences between the algorithms, with the Othman model producing higher predictions (22–58.9 µg/m³) than the Mozafari model (16–57.6 µg/m³) Validation showed a significant correlation between satellite image results and field measurements, with the smallest RMSE of 76.35 (Mozafari, road type 4/1UD) and the largest of 178.82 (Mozafari, road type 2/2UD). This study contributes to the development of satellite-based air quality monitoring methods, particularly in urban areas with limited conventional monitoring instruments. The results are expected to form the basis for environmental policy-making, more sustainable urban planning, and increased public awareness of the impacts of air pollution."]

["Analysis of SO₂ and NO₂ Air Quality Parameters Based on Satellite Images in the Cement Industrial Area", "2025", "This study discusses air quality in cement industrial areas with a focus on two main parameters, namely Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) and Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂). The cement industry is known as one of the largest contributors to pollutant emissions, which can reduce air quality and endanger the health of surrounding communities. Given the limited number of air monitoring stations, this study uses Landsat 8 satellite imagery processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE) as an alternative to monitor air conditions spatially and temporally. This research method involved extracting land surface temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 SR Collection 2 Level 2 images, then estimating SO₂ and NO₂ concentrations using the Mahardianti et al. (2024) algorithm. This satellite data was then validated with field measurements (October 2023 Test Results Report) using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) test to assess the accuracy of the estimation results. The results of the study show that: SO₂ concentrations ranged from 73.10 µg/m³ to 204.18 µg/m³, with the highest distribution in active production areas such as kilns and cement factories. NO₂ concentrations ranged from 22.23 µg/m³ to 75.62 µg/m³ Based on the Air Pollution Standard Index (ISPU) classification, NO₂ was mostly in the “Good” category, while SO₂ was mostly in the “Moderate” to “Unhealthy” category, with the highest ISPU value reaching 169.54 µg/m³ (Unhealthy) for SO₂ and 59.80 µg/m³ (Good) for NO₂. Overall, this study confirms that the use of satellite imagery through GEE can be an effective method for monitoring air quality in industrial areas, especially in regions with limited field monitoring data availability."]

["Air Quality Analysis for Ammonia (NH3) Parameters in the Tamangapa Landfill Area", "2025", "This study is entitled “Air Quality Analysis for Ammonia (NH₃) Parameters in the Tamangapa Landfill Area.” The background of this study is the high amount of organic waste in the Tamangapa landfill in Makassar, which has the potential to produce ammonia (NH₃) gas through the decomposition process. NH₃ gas is toxic, has a pungent odor, and can cause health problems even in low concentrations. The purpose of this study is to analyze NH₃ concentrations in the Tamangapa landfill area and their relationship with meteorological factors (temperature, humidity, air pressure, and wind speed). The study was conducted at five observation points within a radius of 0-1000 meters from the landfill at intervals in the morning, afternoon, evening, and night. Air samples were collected in accordance with the SNI 19-7119.1-2005 standard and then tested in a laboratory using spectrophotometry. The measurement data were visualized using ArcGIS and statistically analyzed using normality tests and Pearson's correlation through SPSS. The results showed that the highest NH₃ concentration was found at the core point of the landfill (point 3), namely 5.885 ppm at night, exceeding the quality standard of 2 ppm based on Minister of Environment Decree No. 50 of 1996. Meanwhile, points 1, 2, 4, and 5 (500–1000 m from the landfill) were still below the threshold. Meteorological analysis showed that humidity and air pressure had a significant effect in reducing NH₃ concentrations, while wind speed and direction played a role in its dispersion, and temperature had a weak effect but tended to increase concentrations at high temperatures. Point 3 Based on the diagram above, it can be seen that there is a correlation between several meteorological data variables, both directly and inversely proportional, although it is not classified as a significant correlation. It can be seen that for meteorological temperature data in the graph above, there is a direct relationship with concentration. This is because when the temperature is high, the concentration of ammonia at the landfill will increase due to evaporation, so that more concentration is dispersed to points 1, 2, 4 and 5, unlike point 3 where the correlation between temperature and concentration is inverse. This is because higher temperatures cause ammonia to evaporate upward, thereby reducing the ammonia concentration at point 3. In conclusion, air pollution by ammonia gas is concentrated within the core area of the landfill and has not spread significantly beyond a radius of 1000 meters. This study emphasizes the importance of regular air quality monitoring at landfills, as well as the need for mitigation efforts to reduce the impact of pollutants on the health of the surrounding community."]

["Noise Level Analysis On Type 6/2D Roads in Makassar City", "2025", "This study is entitled “Analysis of Noise Levels on 6/2 D Roads in Makassar City” conducted by Chozy Muharnitami Putri (2025). The background of this study stems from the increasing number of vehicles in Makassar City, especially two-wheeled vehicles and passenger cars, which has led to an increase in noise on urban roads. The 6/2 D type road was chosen because it is a major arterial road with six lanes in two directions with a median strip, and is the center of economic, commercial, and service activities, resulting in heavy traffic throughout the day. This study aims to analyze the characteristics of noise levels and determine the level of traffic noise on 6/2 D type roads. The research methods included noise measurement using the Decibel X Pro application on smartphones, accompanied by recording vehicle volume with a multi-counter and vehicle speed with a speed gun. Measurements were taken for 14 hours (07:00–20:00 WITA) at six main road points, namely Jalan Veteran Utara, Jalan Perintis Kemerdekaan, Jalan Urip Sumoharjo, Jalan Boulevard, Jalan Boulevard Center Point of Indonesia, and Jalan Letnan Jendral Hertasning. The results of the study show that traffic noise levels ranged from 66.4 to 77.3 dB. The equivalent daily noise value (LAeq,day) at most points exceeded the noise quality standard for commercial and service areas of 70 dB in accordance with Minister of Environment Decree No. 48 of 1996. The high noise levels are influenced by vehicle volume, the dominance of two-wheeled vehicles, speed, and the use of horns. The highest Leqday noise level on a 6/2 D type road in Makassar City is on Urip Sumoharjo Road, which is 77.39 dB. This can be influenced by vehicle volume parameters. Based on the measurement results, the highest vehicle volume on the 6/2 D type road in Makassar City is on Urip Sumoharjo Road, which is 119,384 units. The lowest Leqday noise level on the 6/2 D type road in Makassar City is on Boulevard Center Point of Indonesia Road, which is 66.48 dB. This may be influenced by vehicle volume parameters. Based on the measurement results, the highest vehicle volume on a 6/2 D type road in Makassar City was on Boulevard Center Point of Indonesia Road, which was 12,700 units, there is a linear relationship between noise levels and increasing vehicle volume. The higher the traffic volume on a road, the higher the noise level (Ariyadi, 2023). The following graph shows the relationship between the Leqday noise level and vehicle volume. In conclusion, traffic noise on the 6/2 D road in Makassar City has exceeded the quality standard threshold, which has the potential to disrupt public health and comfort. Therefore, the results of this study are expected to be used as evaluation material for the local government in formulating noise control policies, spatial planning, and traffic management in Makassar City."]

["Modeling CO Dispersion from Motor Vehicle Emissions in Makassar City", "2025", "This study shows that the concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) in the ambient air of Makassar City is still within the safe category. Field measurements show that CO concentrations range from 229 to 1,664 µg/m³, while modeling results using AERMOD show a range of 275 to 1,320 µg/m³. This value is still far below the ambient air quality standard according to Government Regulation No. 22 of 2021, which is 10,000 µg/m³ for a 1-hour average. Motor vehicle emissions in Makassar City ranged from 0.01 to 35.53 grams/second, with the largest contribution coming from motorcycles due to their dominant number, followed by passenger cars and heavy vehicles. Emissions concentrations and loads are higher on busy arterial roads, such as Jalan AP Pettarani, Urip Sumoharjo, Sultan Alauddin, and Perintis Kemerdekaan. AERMOD dispersion modeling results also show that CO dispersion follows the prevailing wind direction, namely to the northwest, and that concentrations decrease with distance from the road source. Overall, the air quality of Makassar City for the CO parameter is still good, but the potential for increased pollution in the future is quite large in line with the growth in the number of motor vehicles. Therefore, routine monitoring, development of public transportation, and vehicle emission control policies are needed to maintain air quality."]

["Analysis of the Relationship between Particulate Matter (PM10) and Vehicle Volume on Type 6/2 and 2/2 Roads", "2025", "This study analyzes the relationship between Particulate Matter (PM₁₀) concentration and vehicle volume on type 6/2 roads (six-lane arterial roads) and type 2/2 roads (two-lane collector roads) in Makassar City. Data was obtained from 16 measurement points during four time intervals (morning, afternoon, evening, and night). The results of the study show that: The highest vehicle volume came from motorcycles, followed by light vehicles, then heavy vehicles. PM₁₀ concentrations at several points exceeded ambient air quality standards (75 µg/m³ per 24 hours, PP No. 22 of 2021), with the highest values reaching 257.99 µg/m³ on type 6/2 roads and 250.77 µg/m³ on type 2/2 roads. Regression analysis shows that the relationship between vehicle volume and PM₁₀ concentration varies: linear regression gives a low correlation, while non-linear polynomial regression shows a stronger relationship. In addition to vehicle volume, other factors such as meteorological conditions, land use, and vegetation around roads also affect PM₁₀ concentrations. The main conclusion is that an increase in vehicle volume, especially during rush hour and on high-capacity roads, contributes significantly to an increase in PM₁₀ concentrations. However, air pollution is not only influenced by traffic but also by environmental factors."]

["Air Quality Parameter Modeling Based on Satellite Imagery in Makassar City", "2025", "This study aims to combine remote sensing data and field measurements to develop a mathematical model capable of accurately predicting the distribution of NO₂, CO₂, and PM₂. This model will combine atmospheric correction and spatial analysis approaches, utilizing the advantages of satellite spatial-temporal resolution that can cover large areas on a regular basis. ["Analysis of PM10 Air Quality Parameters Based on Satellite Images in the Cement Industry Area", "2025", "Important issue regarding air pollution caused by industrial activities, particularly the cement industry, which is known as one of the largest contributors to gas and particle emissions in the world. This industry has a high energy intensity in its production processes and uses fuels such as coal, which produce emissions including carbon monoxide (CO), suspended particles like PM₁₀, and other harmful gases that negatively impact air quality and public health. These pollutants can cause various health issues such as dizziness, nausea, headaches, and even serious disorders of the respiratory and cardiovascular systems. In this context, air quality monitoring is crucial for detecting and controlling the spread of pollutants, especially in areas with high industrial activity. However, manual or conventional monitoring has limitations in terms of coverage area, cost-effectiveness, and data collection frequency. Therefore, remote sensing technology using satellite imagery offers a more efficient and comprehensive alternative solution for spatially and temporally monitoring air quality. This study aims to analyze the concentration of air quality parameters, specifically PM₁₀ and CO, using Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 satellite imagery, which have sufficient spatial and spectral resolution for mapping air pollution in industrial areas. Additionally, another objective is to determine the category of air pollution levels based on the conversion of concentration values into the Air Pollution Index (API), which serves as a reference for assessing the level of air hazards to humans and the environment. This study was conducted in the Semen X Industrial Area, selected due to its high production intensity and suspected to be one of the primary sources of air pollution. The methods used in this study involved several stages, starting with the collection of satellite imagery data through Sentinel Hub and USGS Earth Explorer, followed by geometric, atmospheric, and radiometric corrections to the imagery, and processing using pollutant concentration estimation algorithms such as the Othman and Mozafari algorithms for PM₁₀, and the Somvanshi algorithm for CO. The data obtained from the processing results were then validated with direct measurement data from the cement industry as an accuracy test using the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) method. The results of this study indicate an increase in PM₁₀ concentrations from 2023 to 2024. In 2023, the average PM₁₀ concentration was recorded at 47.69 µg/m³, while in 2024 it increased to 53.61 µg/m³. Meanwhile, CO concentrations remained stable in both years, ranging between an average of 83.22–83.63 µg/m³. After conversion to ISPU, the PM₁₀ concentration falls into the “moderate” category with a maximum value of 50.73, indicating that air quality is still acceptable to humans but begins to have an impact on sensitive groups. On the other hand, the CO parameter shows an ISPU result of 1.04, which falls into the “good” category, indicating no significant risk to human health at that level. Validation of the results using the RMSE test yielded a value of 13.98, indicating that the satellite image estimates have a sufficiently good level of proximity to the actual direct measurement data on-site. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the use of remote sensing technology with a satellite image approach has proven effective in analyzing and monitoring air quality parameters spatially and temporally, especially in industrial areas such as cement regions. This method allows for faster, more efficient, and wider-ranging monitoring compared to conventional methods. This study also highlights the importance of integrating satellite data with field data as validation to obtain more accurate results. The findings of this study are expected to serve as a basis for environmental policy-making and to raise awareness of the importance of air quality monitoring, particularly in areas with high industrial activity. Additionally, this research contributes to the development of technology-based monitoring methods for sustainable application in Indonesia's environmental management systems."]

In a clinical context, biofilm formation significantly complicates treatment, as bacteria in biofilms exhibit heightened resistance to antibiotics—up to 1,000 times greater than their planktonic counterparts. Superbugs, such as Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, are often associated with biofilm infections, leading to increased morbidity and healthcare costs. This research aims to address the following questions: What are the key mechanisms underlying biofilm formation and maintenance? How do biofilms contribute to antibiotic resistance in superbugs? Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Escherichia coli (especially Extended Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL) producers), and Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), are associated with increased morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. MALDI-TOF MS has emerged as a powerful tool for microbial identification due to its speed, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness Objective: The primary aim of this research is to enhance awareness and understanding of biofilm infections and the challenges posed by superbugs among healthcare professionals, patients, and the general public. This will be achieved through the following specific objectives: Increase Knowledge: Educate stakeholders about the nature of biofilms, their formation, and their role in persistent infections caused by superbugs. This includes understanding the mechanisms that allow biofilm-forming bacteria to resist treatment. Highlight Clinical Implications: Emphasize the impact of biofilm-associated infections on patient outcomes, healthcare costs, and the challenges in diagnosis and treatment. This includes discussing the importance of early detection and appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Engage the Community: Mobilize community efforts to raise awareness about antibiotic resistance and the importance of responsible antibiotic use to prevent the emergence of superbugs. ["From Fish to Future Bones: How Local Marine Resources Could Transform Children’s Health", "MAKASSAR, Indonesia Apr 09 2026/adhentisrg/-What if the secret to stronger bones in children lies not in expensive supplements, but in everyday marine resources like anchovies and shrimp shells? A recent scientific study reveals an exciting possibility: turning these natural ingredients into advanced nanomaterials may significantly improve bone growth and health. Bone development is a crucial part of childhood. During this period, the body builds what scientists call “peak bone mass,” which determines bone strength for life. Poor nutrition—especially low calcium intake—can lead to weaker bones, increasing the risk of health problems later. This is where innovation meets tradition. A study titled “Combination of anchovy nanocalcium and shrimp shell nanochitosan on mandibular growth and density in young rats (an in vivo on Rattus norvegicus)” explores how local Indonesian resources can be transformed into powerful health solutions. Published in the Journal of Medicinal and Pharmaceutical Chemistry Research by Sami Publishing Company in 2026, this research highlights how anchovies (rich in calcium) and shrimp shells (rich in chitosan) can be processed into nanoparticles for better absorption in the body. Unlike regular calcium, which is only partially absorbed, nanocalcium is much smaller in size, allowing it to enter the body more efficiently. Meanwhile, nanochitosan not only supports bone formation but also has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. When combined, these two substances work synergistically to enhance bone density, growth, and strength. In the study, young rats were given different treatments, and the group receiving the combination of anchovy nanocalcium and shrimp shell nanochitosan showed the most significant improvement in mandibular (jaw) bone growth. Their bones were denser, longer, and heavier compared to other groups. This suggests a promising future for natural, affordable, and locally sourced health interventions. Beyond science, this innovation connects directly to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3: Good Health and Well-being . By utilizing accessible marine resources, communities—especially in coastal regions—can develop cost-effective nutritional solutions to support children’s growth. This approach not only improves health outcomes but also promotes sustainable use of local biodiversity. Moreover, this research opens opportunities for integrating health, education, and innovation. Educating communities about the benefits of local nutrition aligns with SDG 4 (Quality Education), while transforming waste like shrimp shells into valuable products supports environmental sustainability (SDG 14 and 15). The implications are clear: solutions to global health challenges do not always require high-cost technologies. Sometimes, they are already available in our surroundings—waiting to be rediscovered through science. ["Biomonitoring of Transplacental Transfer of Microplastics in Pregnant Women as an Effort to Control Microplastic Hazards in Mothers and Children", "Grant of Postgraduate Research from Indonesian Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology (2023) Amount: IDR. 28.500.000,- Abstract Microplastics may be present in food and drinks from various sources, exposing pregnant women to these particles. Consumption of contaminated food can lead to the ingestion of microplastics by pregnant women, potentially causing adverse health effects on the fetus. This study aims to investigate the presence of microplastics in the stools of pregnant women. The research was conducted in the Makassar City region of South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Thirty healthy pregnant women from two community health centers, named Pattingalloang and Jumpandang Baru, participated in the study. Their stools were analyzed using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) microspectroscopy to detect the presence of microplastics. The analysis revealed the presence of a total of 359 microplastics in the participants\\' stools, with particle counts ranging from 4 to 21 and sizes ranging from 0.2-4.9 mm per 25 grams of stool. The polymers identified included Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET), Polyamide/Nylon, Polyethylene Chlorinated, HDPE, and Ethylene Propylene. The amount of microplastics varied significantly among groups with different levels of seafood consumption. It is conclude that Some microplastics polymers have been identified in Indonesian pregnants women’ stool."]

["The Effect of Yellow Pumpkin Seed (Cucurbita Moschata) Capsules on Dietary Intake and Hemoglobin Levels in Pregnant Women with Chronic Energy Deficiency (Current Project)", "This study investigates the potential benefits of yellow pumpkin seed (Cucurbita moschata) capsules, which are rich in essential nutrients, on improving dietary intake and hemoglobin levels among pregnant women suffering from chronic energy deficiency (CED). ​Pregnant women with CED are at higher risk of malnutrition and anemia due to insufficient energy and nutrient intake, potentially compromising maternal and fetal health. ​ Yellow pumpkin seeds are a natural source of protein, iron, zinc, and other micronutrients that contribute to increased hemoglobin synthesis and better overall nutritional status. By providing an intervention using these capsules, this research aims to evaluate their impact on improving maternal dietary intake and correcting anemia, thus offering a potential alternative or complementary nutritional strategy for at-risk populations. The primary investigator conducting this study will be Besse, a Master\\'s student specializing in nutritional science, under the close guidance and mentorship of Prof. Aminuddin. ​This research aims to explore the nutritional potential of yellow pumpkin seed capsules in improving dietary intake and hemoglobin levels, addressing the critical issue of malnutrition and anemia in pregnant women with chronic energy deficiency."]

["Development of Noodles Made from Yellow Pumpkin Leaves and Seaweed as an Alternative for Preventing Anemia in Adolescent Girls (Current Project)", "This research explores the potential health benefits of incorporating yellow pumpkin leaves and seaweed into noodles, with the aim of addressing iron-deficiency anaemia prevalent among adolescent girls.​ The study is especially pertinent considering the nutritional challenges faced in this demographic group, offering a palatable and accessible dietary option to improve iron intake. In this research, the nutritional profile of yellow pumpkin leaves and seaweed is examined, highlighting their rich content of vital nutrients such as iron and other vitamins beneficial for blood health. The research also evaluates acceptance, micronutrient content, and the shelf-life of developed noodles. The process involves formulating noodles that retain the nutrient density of these ingredients while ensuring that taste and texture appeal to young consumers. Under Prof Aminuddin supervision, Baiq and Zaitun seeks not only to fortify a common dietary staple but also to provide a sustainable and culturally acceptable food solution that could be implemented on a large scale. This research aims to set a precedent for using easily accessible, locally and readily available resources in combating public health issues. The results of this study could potentially influence policy and inspire further research into alternative food-based interventions for anaemia and other deficiencies. Overall, this innovative approach emphasises the role of diet in preventive healthcare and the importance of tailoring nutritional strategies to meet the needs of specific at-risk populations, particularly young females highly susceptible to iron deficiency anaemia."]

["Development of Yellow Pumpkin Seeds (Cucurbita Moschata Durch) as a Healthy Snack to Address Zinc Deficiency in School Children", "The project is focused on utilizing the nutritional potential of yellow pumpkin seeds to combat zinc deficiency among school-aged children. Zinc deficiency is a prevalent issue that can negatively impact growth, cognitive function, and immune health in children. Yellow pumpkin seeds are a potent source of zinc, containing other essential nutrients like magnesium, phosphorus, and healthy fats that support overall health and development. The project involves developing a tasty and appealing snack for children, leveraging the natural flavor and nutritional content of pumpkin seeds. This initiative seeks to integrate these snacks into children\\'s daily diets as snacks to enhance zinc intake. We expect this can address deficiencies without the need for artificial supplements. By focusing on a food-based approach, the aim is to improve children\\'s nutrition sustainably and naturally. The project will ensure that the snacks are both delicious and beneficial to children\\'s health. By highlighting the benefits of pumpkin seeds as an accessible and effective intervention, this project aims to contribute significantly to improving nutritional outcomes for children at risk of zinc deficiency."]

["Effectiveness of Giving Yellow Pumpkin Seed Biscuits (Cucurbita Moschata Durch) to Pregnant Women to Prevent Stunting in the Stunting Locus Area of ​​Bone Regency, South Sulawesi", "The project titled \"Effectiveness of Giving Yellow Pumpkin Seed Biscuits (Cucurbita Moschata Durch) to Pregnant Women to Prevent Stunting in the Stunting Locus Area of ​​Bone Regency, South Sulawesi\" is designed to address stunting by leveraging the nutritional benefits of pumpkin seeds. Stunting in children can often be traced back to maternal malnutrition during pregnancy, affecting fetal growth and development. This study aims to determine the effectiveness of pumpkin seed biscuits as a dietary intervention to improve the nutritional intake of pregnant women. We expect these pumpkin seed biscuits to enhance the nutritional status of pregnant women, particularly focusing on micronutrients like zinc and iron, which are critical during pregnancy. ​Improved maternal nutrition is expected to contribute to better fetal health, thus reducing the risk of stunting. The biscuits offer an accessible and culturally acceptable means of fortifying the diets of pregnant women, combining traditional food sources with enhanced nutritional value. The study involves a controlled trial where pregnant women are supplemented with these fortified biscuits, and their nutritional markers are monitored throughout the pregnancy and postpartum. The goal is to assess the impact on birth outcomes, particularly in reducing incidents of low birth weight and subsequent stunting in newborns. This project is significant for public health, providing an innovative approach to combatting stunting in high-risk areas."]

["The Effect of Giving Yellow Pumpkin Seed Extract Capsules (Cucurbita Moschata Durch) on Nutritional Status and Hemoglobin in Pregnant Women in Preventing Stunting in Stunting Locus Village, Bone Regency", "Our project was designed to offer alternative nutritional intervention to combat stunting. Stunting, a critical public health concern, results from chronic malnutrition, especially during the first 1,000 days of life, impacting children's physical and cognitive development. Yellow pumpkin seeds are rich in essential nutrients, including proteins, minerals, and vitamins, which can significantly benefit pregnant women, enhancing their nutritional status and hemoglobin levels. This study will investigate the administration of pumpkin seed extract capsules to pregnant women, focusing on their impact on nutritional markers and hemoglobin levels. By enhancing maternal health, the project seeks to create a positive prenatal environment that supports healthy fetal growth, subsequently reducing the risk of stunting. The project undertook extracting active nutrients, capsule formulation, and monitored supplementation in a targeted population of expectant mothers in Bone Regency. The outcome will be measured through pre-and post-supplementation assessments of nutritional and hemoglobin status. ​By providing a natural, effective prenatal supplement, this project aims to contribute toward reducing stunting and promoting healthier future generations within the community."]

["Formulation of Pumpkin Seed Extract Capsules (Cucurbita Moschata Durch) to Lower Blood Pressure in Hypertension Patients in the Tamalanrea Health Center Area", "This project was aimed at developing an innovative nutritional intervention for managing hypertension. Hypertension, a prevalent health issue, often requires ongoing medication, and alternative treatments such as those derived from natural sources are increasingly sought after. Pumpkin seeds ( Cucurbita moschata ) are recognized for their high content of beneficial phytochemicals like phytoestrogens, antioxidants, and essential fatty acids, which have shown potential in reducing blood pressure. This research will focus on formulating a pumpkin seed extract capsule and determining optimal extract dosage while ensuring bioavailability and patient compliance. Key phases of the project will include extraction of active compounds, selection of appropriate excipients, capsule production, and rigorous quality control testing. ​The final product aims to offer a natural, side-effect-free alternative that can complement existing hypertension therapies. The project's effectiveness was tested through a clinical trial conducted with patients at the Tamalanrea Health Center. This trial evaluated the capsules' impact on blood pressure alongside safety and patient satisfaction metrics."]

["Pumpkin Seed Coffee Formulation as a Healthy Drink Rich in Antioxidants", "This research was dedicated to developing a coffee-like beverage derived from pumpkin seeds, focusing on harnessing their remarkable antioxidant capacities. This study was aimed to formulate a drink that mirrors the sensory appeal of coffee while delivering enhanced health benefits associated with antioxidants. The research’s goal is to create a nutritious beverage that aligns with dietary preferences. This project holds promise in contributing to the development of innovative health-driven beverages, offering consumers a functional drink that supports overall well-being and caters to the increasing demand for antioxidant-rich diets."]

["The Effect of Combination of Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs and Pumpkin Seed Capsules on the Amount of Bacteria in Sputum of TB Patients in Majene Regency", "The study was aimed at exploring the potential effects of combining traditional anti-tuberculosis drugs with pumpkin seed capsules. By analysing sputum samples, the study seeks to measure the bacterial load in tuberculosis patients undergoing this combined treatment approach. The intent is to determine if the inclusion of pumpkin seed capsules, known for their nutritional benefits and possible antimicrobial properties, can reduce the bacterial counts more effectively than traditional drug therapy alone. A hypothesis is that the bioactive compounds in pumpkin seeds could potentially support immune function, contributing to a faster reduction in the bacterial load. ​The significance of this study lies in its potential to improve tuberculosis treatment protocols, particularly in regions like Majene Regency.​ This research could also lead to reduced treatment durations and improved outcomes for patients, aligning with public health goals to combat tuberculosis more efficiently."]

["Measurement of Hospital Resilience in Local Government-owned Hospitals in South Sulawesi Province", "2024", "Resilience at the organizational level or known as organizational resilience is more developed in the field of modern business and management where companies potentially face various obstacles related to policies, economic crises and changes in market mechanisms. ["Determinants of occupational health and safety problems among seaweed workers in takalar regency", "Seaweed industry is one of the most growing marine sector of industry in South Sulawesi. It is generally assumed that, seaweed workers are vulnerable to experience workplace injury and occupational disease. This study aims to explore determinants of occupational safety and health (OSH) problems among seaweed workers in Takalar District, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The research is a quantitative study using cross sectional study design. Questionnaires survey were distributed among 105 seaweed workers from four districts in Takalar Regency. The data were analyzed using chi-square test and Odds Ratio (OR) analysis. The results showed that the main OHS problems among seaweed workers were work injury, work fatigue, and low back pain. Work fatigue was associated with pulse > average, work period > 1 year and duration of sunlight exposure > average. Meanwhile, work injury was associated with being female, work period > 1 year and working > 8 hours. Moreover, type of work such as maintenance, processing and all type of work were associated with low back pain. This study recommends to local government and other stakeholders to conduct interventions based on the findings of this research. A further research is needed to provide a longitudinal database on OSH problems among this subgroup of workers that help decision makers to plan a better and effective intervention."]

["Seaweed farmers and work fatigue: A mixed-method approach", "BACKGROUND: In Indonesia, particularly in the coastal area, there is a growing number of seaweed farmers who work in the informal sector as a home-based industry. It is generally assumed that this sub-group of workers is also experiencing work fatigue. AIM: This research aims to explore information-related factors that are associated with fatigue among seaweed workers. METHODS: The study was conducted in Takalar Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The research used a mixedmethod design combining quantitative and qualitative approach. One hundred sixty-one samples were taken from four districts Mangarabombang, Mappakasunggu, Sanrobone, and North Galesong. RESULTS: More than half of the respondents feel fatigue 67.1%. Furthermore, based on bivariate analysis, it was found that there were significant associations between work hour p = 0.041 and work period p = 0.031 with work fatigue. For the qualitative approach, three focus group discussions were conducted to explore more information related to factors that were found associated with work fatigue from the quantitative study. This research found that a large number of employees experienced work fatigue. CONCLUSION: The factor that associated with work fatigue is work hour and work period. It is suggested that health providers and stakeholders related need to pay attention to this subgroup of the working population regarding their occupational health and safety problems."]

["Work Fatigue Among Seaweed Workers in Takalar District", "Fatigue is a common condition for all workers after doing their job One of the informal sectors that has not yet received adequate occupational health services is seaweed workers. This research aims to determine the relationship between age, working time, work period, work attitude, workload, and work process of workplace fatigue on seaweed workers in Takalar district. The type of this research is an analytical observational with a cross sectional study approach. The samples in this study were 74 respondents using purposive sampling techniques. Data was obtained using the Work Fatigue Measurement Tool Questionnaire for fatigue and a Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) Questionnaire sheet for work attitude. Chi-Square test was used to analise the relationship between variables. The results showed that workers experienced 27% working fatigue and 73% of workers who did not experience work fatigue. As for the relationship between age (p=0.006) and work process (p=0.030) with work fatigue, and no relationship between the length of work (p=0.183), the working period (p=0.429), the working attitude (p=0.319), and the workload (p=0.080) with work fatigue. It is suggested that worker need to pay attention to have sufficient rest time and stretch in between jobs in order to prevent work fatigue."]

["Relation of body mass index and work posture to musculoskeletal disorders among fishermen", "Objective: In this study, we researched to determine the relationship between body mass index (BMI) and work posture/position with the musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) in fishermen. Method: This type of research is analytic survey research with a cross-sectional study. There were 224 people as the population in this study with 56 samples as respondents. Nordic Body Map (NBM) and Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) were used as a questionnaire instrument. Results: The result of the Chi-square test shows that the BMI variable has a p-value of p = 0.848 where the p-value is p > 0.05. This means BMI has no significant relationship with MSD. Meanwhile, the work posture/position variable has a p-value of p = 0.000 where the p-value is p < 0.05, which means that there is a significant relationship with MSD. Conclusions: BMI was not associated with MSD. This is possible because fishermen who have normal and abnormal BMI both have complaints of MSD. Meanwhile, work posture/position has a significant relationship with complaints of MSD in fishermen. This is because the posture of fishermen when working with tools when doing research looks very risky."]

["Musculoskeletal disorders problems and its relation to age, working periods, and smoking habit among fishermen", "Objective: In this study, we conducted a research to determine the relationship between ages, working period, and smoking habit with the musculoskeletal disorder in fishermen. Method: This type of research is analytic survey research with a cross-sectional study. The population in this study totaled 224 people with 56 samples as respondents. Nordic Body Map (NBM) and Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) were used as a questionnaire instrument. Results: The result showed that the age variable has p = 0.658 and the smoking habit has p = 1.000, this indicates that age and smoking habit variables do not have a significant relationship with musculoskeletal disorders. Meanwhile, the working period variable has a result of p = 0.015, it can be said that the work period has a significant relationship with musculoskeletal disorders. Conclusion: The respondents who were quite old were still fit for work and did not have as many musculoskeletal complaints as they should be for their age. Likewise with the smoking habit of fishermen who are more enthusiastic and motivated to work. Meanwhile, the work period has more influence on the complaints of musculoskeletal disorders among fishermen."]

["Relation Between Work Duration and Type of Work With Musculoskeletal Disorders of Fishermen in Occupational Health Efforts Post Fishermen of Maros Regency", "Musculoskeletal disorders that occur in workers are influenced by factors. The factors highlighted in this study are the length of work and type of work. This study aims to determine the relationship between work duration and type of work with musculoskeletal disorders in fishermen in the UKK (Occupational Health Efforts) Post, Maros Regency. This type of research is analytic survey research with cross-sectional study/cross-sectional design. The population in this study totaled 224 people. Sampling when this research took place was carried out by accidental sampling. The results of this study indicate that there is a significant relationship between the length of work with musculoskeletal disorders in fishermen at the UKK post of fishermen in Maros Regency. There is a significant relationship between the types of work with musculoskeletal disorders in fishermen at the UKK fishermen post in Maros Regency. Length of work is the factor that has the greatest influence on musculoskeletal disorders in fishermen at the fishermen\\'s UKK post in Maros Regency. In order to do stretches both before and after every activity, for fishermen aged> 45 years, be careful in carrying out activities and minimize awkward attitudes/work positions and always participate in every meeting, guidance, and health examination conducted by the occupational health program manager."]

["The Effect of Safety Climate on Safety Behavior with Safety Motivation as An Intervening Variable on Contractor Workers in PT X", "Safety climate in the workplace and safety behaviour of workers need attention to be able to assess what factors are the causes of safe action for workers. This study aims to determine the effect of safety climate on safety behaviour with safety motivation as an intervening variable on contractor workers at PT X. The type of research is analytical observational with a cross sectional design. Questionnaires were given to 380 respondents. The data were analyzed using path analysis to see the direct and indirect effects of safety climate on safety behaviour. The results showed, 361 respondents (95%) with good safety climate, 367 respondents (96.9%) with good safety motivation, and 348 respondents (91%) with good safety behaviour. The path analysis showed that there was no direct influence of safety climate on safety behaviour in contractor workers at PT X (p value >0.05). However, the safety climate indirectly affects safety behaviour through safety motivation (p value = 0.001). It is recommended to workers that they need to maintain and increase their motivation so the safe work behaviour will still create."]

["Cadre Assistance in Effort to Reduce the Unmet Need for Contraception in Childbearing Age Couples in Coppo Village, Barru District, Barru Regency", "Health issues in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are integrated into one goal, specifically goal number three, which aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages. One of the objectives of the Family Planning Program is to decrease the incidence of unmet need, a factor contributing to rising maternal mortality rates and population growth in Indonesia. Unmet need refers to the percentage of women of childbearing age who wish to stop or delay childbirth for at least two years but are not using contraception. This phenomenon is particularly prevalent in developing countries and is considered an indicator of the success of family planning programs. This service activity aims to enhance the understanding and knowledge of couples of childbearing age about family planning and contraception through cadre assistance."]

["Factors Associated with Tetanus Toxoid Immunization in Pregnant Women in Polewali Village", "Immunization is a method used to prevent and effectively reduce the number of devastating disease infections globally. Tetanus Toxoid immunization in pregnant women or women of childbearing age can reduce the risk of neonatal tetanus by 94%. Implementation of tetanus toxoid immunization in Indonesia based on profile Indonesia\\'s health in 2019 was 64.88% which is still less than the figure 80% to maintain ETMN status. This research aims to determine related factors with tetanus toxoid immunization in pregnant women in Polewali sub-district."]

["Factors Associated with Reproductive Health Attitudes and Behavior of Overseas Female Students in Makassar City", "Reproductive health problems are closely related to sexual behavior, especially among teenagers. Sexual experience is reported to be higher in women and men aged 20-24 years.
